data.title: We moved from AWS to Hetzner, saved 90%, kept ISO 27001 with Ansible
data.author: sksjvsla
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了一家丹麦公司从AWS迁移到欧洲云服务提供商的经历，成功将ISO 27001认证成本降低了90%，同时解决了GDPR合规问题。主要驱动力包括对美国政府可能获取数据的担忧以及AWS高昂费用的压力。通过迁移到Hetzner和OVHcloud等欧洲供应商，公司实现了真正的数据主权、大幅削减了成本，并通过自主构建的自动化基础设施提高了安全性和可控性。使用Ansible实现合规管理，结合Prometheus、Grafana和Loki进行监控，公司不仅保持了ISO 27001认证，还提升了安全性和响应速度。这次迁移不仅是一次技术变革，更是一次商业转型，增强了客户信任并节省了大量预算。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：从AWS迁移到自建或替代云服务的成本与收益分析

不同观点：
• jillesvangurp：认为自建服务可能成本更高，尤其是考虑到24x7支持和开发时间等隐性成本。即使能节省费用，也需要更多人力资源支持。同时，认为Terraform对小规模设置来说过于复杂（YAGNI），更偏好Ansible。
• martypitt：通过Prometheus、Grafana和Loki等工具获得了比AWS更好的监控体验，认为AWS的监控服务昂贵且用户体验差。
• Keyframe：关注硬件故障和升级问题，并询问Loki如何处理内存消耗问题，以及是否有替代方案。
• ksec：提到UpCloud作为Hetzner和OVH的替代方案，指出Hetzner使用消费级组件，可能不适合某些企业需求。
• sgt：解释ISO 27001在欧洲的流行和SOC 2在美国的偏好，指出两者在不同地区的相关性和重要性。
• yread：质疑成本节省的实际效果，指出根据描述的费用，可能不需要分布式系统，并询问请求量和用户数。
• jordanbeiber：分享了类似的Azure迁移经验，认为云服务通过复杂的服务抽象增加了运营负担，简化运营更具价值。
• liampulles：认为AWS降低了运营负担，尤其是通过托管服务减少了手动升级和准备工作，虽然费用高，但有其价值。
• cataflam：认为AWS比自建VPS/裸金属更贵是众所周知的事情，但缺少技术细节（如升级和多数据中心备份）和全面的成本分析（特别是人力成本）。
• saltysalt：对Hetzner有正面评价，运行互联网搜索引擎，偏好裸金属。
• 0xjunhao：认为随着Agentic AI的兴起，除非AWS大幅降价，否则迁移到更便宜的提供商是正确的选择。
• sam_lowry_：分享了自己成功从AWS迁移到Hetzner的经验，并表示有意开展“回归基础迁移”业务，但难以找到客户。
• nopakos：提出希望有一个欧洲的CloudFlare。
• hk1337：质疑ISO 27001的实际重要性，认为SSAE 16和其他SSAE标准更受关注。
• louwrentius：认为相关的Medium文章内容较少，更多是宣传和线索生成，不如“Shown HN”帖子有价值。

补充讨论：
- 成本分析的全面性：多个评论提到自建服务或使用替代云服务的总成本不仅包括基础设施费用，还应考虑人力和支持成本。
- 监控问题：部分评论指出AWS的监控服务体验不佳，而自建或使用其他工具（如Prometheus、Grafana）可以获得更好的效果。
- 硬件问题：有评论关注到自建方案中硬件故障和升级的实际操作问题。
- 地域合规性：讨论了不同地区对安全管理标准的偏好，如ISO 27001和SOC 2。
- 市场需求：有人提到虽然很多人讨论迁移，但实际愿意采取行动的客户较少。

44335920.article_content:
European Cloud can makes ISO 27001 easier
Goodbye AWS: How We Kept ISO 27001, Slashed Costs by 90%
The European CTO’s Dilemma: Keeping Compliance outside AWS
Datapult
Follow
4 min read
·
3 hours ago
--
Listen
Share
Earlier this year, I faced a dilemma many tech leaders know well. Our entire infrastructure was built on AWS. We loved their powerful, ISO 27001-certified services. Yet, two critical issues kept me up at night:
The Compliance Black Hole:
It was clear that American cloud providers couldn’t fully shield us from US government jurisdiction. Under the CLOUD Act and FISA, our European customer data was potentially exposed, regardless of the server’s physical location. This undermined our GDPR promises.
The $2,000/Month Question:
While not a fortune for every company, our $24,000 annual bill felt disproportionate to our actual needs. I asked myself: how often does a well-maintained Linux server actually crash? Isn’t RDS just a managed Postgres instance with scripts I could write myself? That $2,000 a month could buy a phenomenal amount of resilient, dedicated hardware in Europe.
This wasn’t just about cost or compliance; it was a strategic risk. Was tying our company’s future to a single US-based provider a responsible choice?
Our story
We are a Danish workforce management company doing employee scheduling. Beyond our ISO 27001 certificate, we have a few legal requirements on our operation as well as we perform overtime compensation salary adjustments and are source of truth for time-and-attendance data. Maintaining the tech side of this, is just like maintaining a bank software: Things must be accounted for, always add up and never be lost.
Born and raised in AWS, many aspects of our legal requirement was architected as AWS native workflows and migrating that to independent alternatives always had to go along with legal requirements.
What You Fear Losing (And What You Actually Lose)
Let’s be honest: leaving AWS feels like walking away from a fortress of convenience. You lose the “magic” of deeply integrated services like Lambda, one-click RDS deployments, and the rich ecosystem of built-in compliance tooling that makes ISO 27001 audits smoother.
Giving this up is the primary source of fear and inaction for most teams. It means trading the comfort of managed services for a higher degree of control and responsibility.
What You Stand to Gain: Sovereignty, Savings, and Sanity
By migrating to European providers like Hetzner and OVHcloud, the gains weren’t just theoretical. They were immediate and strategic.
True Data Sovereignty:
Hosting on European-owned infrastructure gave us undeniable proof of data residency — a game-changer for GDPR audits and ISO 27001 recertification. We could tell our customers exactly where their data was, with no ambiguity.
Radical Cost Efficiency:
Our cloud costs dropped by
90%
. This wasn’t a typo. By replacing expensive managed services with our own automated, self-hosted solutions, our budget became predictable and transparent.
Forced Innovation:
The biggest surprise was how losing AWS’s pre-built tools forced us to get better. We built a powerful infrastructure-as-code setup using Ansible that gave us even tighter security controls and auditability than before.
The Blueprint: Key Lessons for Your Own Migration
This migration taught us invaluable lessons that can serve as a blueprint for others. Here’s the core of our strategy:
Ansible as Your Compliance Engine:
Forget simple compliance checks. With properly structured Ansible playbooks, you can tie every line of your server configuration directly to a specific ISO 27001 Annex A control. Your infrastructure code becomes a self-documenting audit trail.
Monitoring That Rivals AWS:
You don’t need CloudWatch to have enterprise-grade monitoring. A combination of
Prometheus, Grafana, and Loki
allowed us to replicate — and in some ways exceed — the visibility we had on AWS, ensuring faster incident response.
Security-by-Design Becomes Reality:
When there isn’t a pre-made security solution to click on, you build it into the foundation. This “security-by-design” approach, automated with Ansible, makes your ISMS (Information Security Management System) incredibly robust and easy for developers to follow.
The Strategic Impact: Beyond Tech
This wasn’t just a technical project; it was a business transformation.
We minimized our compliance risk
regarding US surveillance laws.
We used our European hosting as a sales tool,
strengthening brand trust.
We returned 90% of our cloud spend to the business
Your Move: Is a Migration Strategy Right for You?
If this story resonates with you, you’re likely asking: “Could we actually do this? What would it cost? What are the hidden risks?”

主要讨论点：从AWS迁移到自建或替代云服务的成本与收益分析

不同观点：
• jillesvangurp：认为自建服务可能成本更高，尤其是考虑到24x7支持和开发时间等隐性成本。即使能节省费用，也需要更多人力资源支持。同时，认为Terraform对小规模设置来说过于复杂（YAGNI），更偏好Ansible。
• martypitt：通过Prometheus、Grafana和Loki等工具获得了比AWS更好的监控体验，认为AWS的监控服务昂贵且用户体验差。
• Keyframe：关注硬件故障和升级问题，并询问Loki如何处理内存消耗问题，以及是否有替代方案。
• ksec：提到UpCloud作为Hetzner和OVH的替代方案，指出Hetzner使用消费级组件，可能不适合某些企业需求。
• sgt：解释ISO 27001在欧洲的流行和SOC 2在美国的偏好，指出两者在不同地区的相关性和重要性。
• yread：质疑成本节省的实际效果，指出根据描述的费用，可能不需要分布式系统，并询问请求量和用户数。
• jordanbeiber：分享了类似的Azure迁移经验，认为云服务通过复杂的服务抽象增加了运营负担，简化运营更具价值。
• liampulles：认为AWS降低了运营负担，尤其是通过托管服务减少了手动升级和准备工作，虽然费用高，但有其价值。
• cataflam：认为AWS比自建VPS/裸金属更贵是众所周知的事情，但缺少技术细节（如升级和多数据中心备份）和全面的成本分析（特别是人力成本）。
• saltysalt：对Hetzner有正面评价，运行互联网搜索引擎，偏好裸金属。
• 0xjunhao：认为随着Agentic AI的兴起，除非AWS大幅降价，否则迁移到更便宜的提供商是正确的选择。

• nopakos：提出希望有一个欧洲的CloudFlare。
• hk1337：质疑ISO 27001的实际重要性，认为SSAE 16和其他SSAE标准更受关注。
• louwrentius：认为相关的Medium文章内容较少，更多是宣传和线索生成，不如“Shown HN”帖子有价值。

- 成本分析的全面性：多个评论提到自建服务或使用替代云服务的总成本不仅包括基础设施费用，还应考虑人力和支持成本。
- 监控问题：部分评论指出AWS的监控服务体验不佳，而自建或使用其他工具（如Prometheus、Grafana）可以获得更好的效果。
- 硬件问题：有评论关注到自建方案中硬件故障和升级的实际操作问题。
- 地域合规性：讨论了不同地区对安全管理标准的偏好，如ISO 27001和SOC 2。

data.title: On memes, mimetic desire, and why it's always that deep
data.author: lawrenceyan
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对文化现象的批判性分析与个人享受之间的关系，以及个体在社会结构中的行为模式。

不同观点：
• [rixed] 认为人们缺乏通过集体行动解决结构性问题的工具，因此往往通过个人道德视角解读这些问题。他还提出，人们通过情感捷径（如符号和道德）相互影响，而不是通过知识。
   
• [Apreche] 认为人们无法质疑自己为何享受某些事物，并将批判性思考与道德谴责混为一谈。他强调自己会严格区分道德判断与质量判断，并认为大多数人无法回答“为什么喜欢某物”的问题。

• [NoboruWataya] 指出对流行文化的深度分析可能有趣且有益，但过度消费这些内容会让人疲惫。他认为，许多流行事物受欢迎正是因为不需要过多思考，过度分析可能削弱享受。他主张人们应根据需要选择是否接触这些分析内容。

• [57473m3n7Fur7h3] 提到在移动端阅读时，由于排版问题，误将号召性内容当作引用，造成困惑。

• [shayway] 享受批判性分析，但认为有些人将这种分析视为道德要求是不合理的。他主张分析的动机应是乐趣，而非道德优越感，并强调好奇心应自然产生，而非被强加。

• [strken] 认为“让人们享受事物”的观点常被用作无法准确反驳时的托辞。他批评对资本主义的无差别批判，指出这种批判的泛滥使其失去说服力。

• [blamestross] 认为 meme 是压缩的沟通形式，通过文化和情境解压缩，让人感到温暖和能动性。

• [mensetmanusman] 提出个体主义的衰落是由于人口结构变化，认为这种心态不会延续到2070年以后。

• [g-r-a-y-d] 简单表达了对火车的喜爱，未参与主要讨论。

补充讨论：
• 引用了 René Girard 的复杂哲学观点，探讨模仿欲望、个体性与冲突的关系，进一步丰富了对文化和个体行为的理解。

争议焦点：
• 是否应通过批判性分析质疑文化现象，还是允许人们不加思考地享受事物。
• 批判性分析是否应被视为一种道德要求，或者仅仅是一种个人选择和乐趣。
• 对资本主义的无差别批判是否有效，以及这种批判是否削弱了分析的说服力。

data.title: Using Microsoft's New CLI Text Editor on Ubuntu
data.author: jandeboevrie
data.article_summary: Microsoft发布了开源命令行文本编辑器**Edit**，是旧版MS-DOS Editor的现代化重制版，使用Rust编写，旨在提供类似VS Code的界面和输入控制。Edit主要面向Windows用户，因为Windows缺乏内置的CLI文本编辑器，但它也可以在Linux和macOS上运行。Edit功能简洁，主打速度和简易性，支持查找替换、字词换行、多文件编辑等基本功能，但没有语法高亮或配色方案。它采用无模式设计，支持鼠标和键盘操作，易于上手。目前，Edit没有官方的Linux安装程序，但可通过GitHub或Snap安装。未来计划加入更多功能，但核心仍是轻量级文本编辑。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Edit文本编辑器在不同操作系统上的使用、技术实现、历史背景及相关工具的讨论

不同观点：
• simonw：分享了如何通过Docker在macOS上运行Edit编辑器，并提供了具体命令和参考链接，强调该方法适用于Apple silicon上的Docker用户。同时提到可以从源码编译Edit。
• felineflock：认为文章混淆了TUI和CLI的概念，指出Edit实际上是1991年MS-DOS 5中EDIT程序的重新实现，并提供了相关的历史背景，如VIM和vi编辑器的出现时间，以及其他历史上的Windows文本编辑器（如EDIT、DR-DOS EDITOR等）。
• hiAndrewQuinn：讨论了常用快捷键（如Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V）的来源和使用，认为这些快捷键应更为普及，特别是在终端中的使用。
• orsenthil：赞赏Edit的易用性和简洁性，认为Linux默认编辑器（如nano, vim, emacs）对新手不够友好，建议引入类似Edit的界面。
• seabrookmx：评价Edit功能简陋，缺乏语法高亮等功能，推荐使用micro编辑器，该编辑器支持CTRL-C/V和鼠标操作。
• czarit：对Edit项目依赖于libc而不是使用Rust社区中常用的crate（如termios）表示不解，认为这种实现方式在Rust世界中非常 unusual。
• jll29：建议将Edit别名为msedit以实现“DOS兼容性”。
• aa-jv：提到PC-Write编辑器，认为其在80年代非常强大，但如今已很少使用，建议将其移植到Linux，可能是一个有趣的项目。
• jmmv：提到自己曾写过一篇关于DOS和Windows编辑器历史的文章，正是由于微软提议重新在Windows中添加文本编辑器引发的讨论。
• posix86：希望Windows终端能够移植到Linux，特别是其对Ctrl+C功能的处理。
• k3vinw：询问Edit是否仅借用了VS Code的键盘快捷键，并希望其能支持LSP和扩展功能。
• declan_roberts：赞赏Edit的UI设计，认为其不同于vim和eMacs，并让人怀念Windows 3.0/DOS时代。
• neoden：询问截图中使用的字体。
• culebron21：提到Norton Commander及其编辑器，讨论了其继任者（如Midnight Commander和FAR Manager），并指出其使用中的一些不便之处。
• tedunangst：幽默地指出老用户对全屏终端编辑器和CLI编辑器的区分感到不满。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：对Edit编辑器的技术实现及其与历史编辑器的比较存在不同看法，部分用户认为Edit简化了使用体验，而另一些用户则关注其功能是否足够强大和完善。
• 历史背景：对MS-DOS时期的文本编辑器（如EDIT和PC-Write）的历史讨论，以及它们在现代操作系统中的潜在价值和移植可能性。
• 快捷键和用户界面：讨论了不同平台上快捷键的普及和一致性问题，以及Edit编辑器的UI设计对用户体验的影响。

44306892.article_content:
If you spend a lot time in a terminal on Linux you’ll have preferred command-line text editor, but Microsoft’s recently announced open-source offering, simply called
Edit
, might be worth checking out — if only so you know you’re not missing out.
Edit
is a remake/reboot of the old
MS-DOS Editor
, updated to suit current sensibilities. Built using Rust, it aims to deliver a user experience that, per its GitHub page, provides
“modern interface and input controls similar to VS Code.”
Microsoft says it made
Edit
“to provide an accessible editor that even users largely unfamiliar with terminals can easily use”
on Windows if/when needed, out-of-the-box (as recent versions of Windows do not include a CLI text editor in recent versions).
The arrival of
Edit
will mean Windows devs aren’t forced to fire up notepad.exe to make a simple shell script edit, but is there any benefit to running the app on Linux?
Note:
When I spotlight apps, tools and utilities on this blog, it’s
not
because I think you (or anyone) “MUST” use them. I simply showcase choices. Whether you choose to use them is up to you.
Why would Linux users use
Edit
?
As straightforward to use as it seems
Windows is the primary target for
Edit
since it lacks a built-in CLI text editor natively so the fact you can use
Edit
on Linux (and macOS) is more of bonus than purpose.
But if you use Linux and
VSCode
your muscle memory might like the fact
Edit
shares many of the latter’s keybindings. This could make it easier to slot in to your workflow compared to
vim
or
nano
(though I stress it’s not a replacement for either of those).
Not that only avowed VSCode fans will see the appeal.
The simplicity of the text-driven UI (TUI) makes it less complex to learn, while the speed of
Edit
, even when seeking across lines in giant 1GB+ files, is impressive — both USPs are by design.
Working with multiple files is easy enough too
Eager to avoid “how to exit vim” memes, Microsoft designed
Edit
as a modeless text editor (as opposed to a multi-mode one like Vim, where you need to learn how to activate different modes and switch between them as needed).
You can
use a mouse or a keyboard
to access menus, select lines or regions of text, position the caret, etc which makes using it feel more intuitive in use than the either/or approach of (admittedly more capable) alternatives.
Edit
offers up a modest, lightweight set of features (and an equally modest footprint: a mere 250kB out of the box, and fast file opening) including:
Find and Replace
(supports
Match Case
&
Regular Expression
)
Word wrap
on resize
(optional)
Set tab/space indentation
Set/change file encoding
Line Feed (LF) or Carriage Return + Line Feed ( CRLF)
Open multiple files
There’s pretty much all there is right now.
Edit
has no syntax highlighting, no range of colour schemes, no command prompt, and few creature comforts common in other command line text editors.
Edit
is designed to edit text, rather than handle complex task better suited to IDEs.
More features are planned, including colour schemes and a settings TUI, so the list of features will grow in time, but as Microsoft’s aim is speed and simplicity, don’t expect too many bells and whistles.
Edit
is open source so anyone can modify, contribute, package or fork it.
How to Run
Edit
on Ubuntu
Edit
is free, open source software that works on Windows, Linux and macOS (so no, you don’t need to using Windows to make use of it).
Right now there is no official “installer” for Linux, and no unofficial DEB of PPA, though
there is a snap
. A couple of Linux distributions now package
Edit
, including Arch Linux, and Manjaro, so if you use one of those, you can install it properly.
To run
Edit
on Ubuntu you can download the latest binary from the
project GitHub releases page
(be sure to select the correct one for your architecture), extract the package,
cd
into the extracted folder, then launch the binary each time you want to use it:
Download the latest release
(link above)
Extract the archive
(right-click in
Nautilus
>
Extract
)
Open a terminal app
(such as the new
Pytxis
in Ubuntu 25.10
)
Navigate to the extracted folder:
cd /path/to/
Run
Edit
directly:
./edit
To install the unofficial snap build use
App Center
(search ‘msedit’) or run
sudo snap install msedit
from the command line, and use
msedit
to launch it. On my laptop, the snap takes ~5 seconds to open. The official binary is instantaneous. YMMV.
From there, the interface is easy enough to figure out.
Give it a try and let me know what you think!
CLI Tools
Edit
Microsoft
Text Editor

主要讨论点：iOS平台上的浏览器内容过滤工具，特别是Firefox对第三方内容过滤的支持问题以及不同广告拦截工具的比较和使用体验。

不同观点：
• [HexDecOctBin] 认为Firefox在iOS上自2019年以来拒绝支持第三方内容过滤器是不合理的，尽管无法使用Gecko引擎，但仍应投入资源争取品牌的用户关注。
• [azretd] 推荐使用Wipr，表示其在跨平台上表现出色，且能有效阻止侵入式广告。

补充讨论：
• [jen729w] 推荐1Blocker，表示其使用体验非常好，且已经使用多年。
• [wao0uuno] 对1Blocker持保留意见，认为其无法完全阻止所有广告。

争议焦点：
• Firefox在iOS平台上缺乏对第三方内容过滤的支持，是否应该投入更多资源以提升其品牌影响力。
• 不同广告拦截工具（如Wipr、1Blocker、uBlock、AdGuard）的比较和选择，用户在使用体验和效果上存在不同看法。

To join the uBlock Origin Lite beta, open the link on your iPhone, iPad, or Mac after you install TestFlight.
Step 1
Get TestFlight
Help developers test beta versions of their apps and App Clips using the

Step 2
View uBlock Origin Lite Beta
**uBO Lite** (uBOL), an efficient [MV3 API-based](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/mv3/intro/) content blocker.
uBOL is entirely declarative, meaning there is no need for a permanent uBOL process for the filtering to occur, and CSS/JS injection-based content filtering is [performed reliably](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/scripting/#method-registerContentScripts) by the browser itself rather than by the extension. This means that uBOL itself does not consume CPU/memory resources while content blocking is ongoing -- uBOL's service worker process is required _only_ when you interact with the popup panel or the option pages.
The default ruleset corresponds to at least uBlock Origin's default filterset:
- uBlock Origin's built-in filter lists
- EasyList
- EasyPrivacy
- Peter Lowe’s Ad and tracking server list
You can add more rulesets by visiting the options page -- click the _Cogs_ icon in the popup panel.

data.title: Discord.com added to EasyList, the biggest adblock filter list
data.author: akyuu
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要报告了一个问题：Discord.com被错误地列入了EasyList的屏蔽列表，导致该网站被阻挡。提交者NanashiTheNameless在2025年6月21日指出，Discord.com出现在EasyList的广告服务器屏蔽列表中，导致其被错误阻挡。虽然Discord是一个消息平台，但其根域名被误分类为第三方广告商。提交者希望修正这个问题，因为除分析或科学部分外，Discord不应该被屏蔽。该问题尚未分配处理人。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：某内容被反复添加的现象及其原因

不同观点：
• **[tchbnl]** 认为应听取贡献者的解释。该贡献者在此平台上非常活跃，反复添加某内容可能有其原因。tchbnl对贡献者的动机持开放态度，希望了解其具体解释。

• **[Alifatisk]** 怀疑该行为可能存在恶意意图。他的论据是该内容在被移除后仍不断被添加，这种反复行为让他猜测是否有人故意为之。

• **[Dah00n]** 认为这一现象没有问题，他将此现象比作聊天世界中的Pinterest，暗示这是一种正常的内容分享或管理方式，没有必要过度担忧。

补充讨论：
• **争议的焦点** 在于该内容被反复添加的行为是否具有恶意。Alifatisk明确表达了对其动机的怀疑，而Dah00n则认为这属于正常现象，无需小题大做。

• **tchbnl** 的立场较为中立，希望通过听取贡献者的解释来进一步判断，而不是立即下结论。

• **例子**：Alifatisk提到了内容被反复添加的事实，而Dah00n则用Pinterest来比喻，认为这种行为类似于一种内容整理和分享的行为。

data.article_summary: SEGA已将九款经典游戏在Android和iOS上免费提供，但即将停止支持。这些游戏包括《Crazy Taxi Classic》、《Shining Force Classics》、《Streets of Rage 2 Classic》等。虽然即将从应用商店下架，但一旦用户下载，游戏可能会永久保留在账户中。这些游戏此前多为付费或包含内购去广告，现已全部免费。SEGA Forever计划已在2023年终止，这些移动移植游戏也将失去支持。用户可在游戏下架前免费领取并继续离线游玩。

These retro SEGA games are now free on Android until they disappear forever
Claim these Sonic, Shining Force, Streets of Rage, and Crazy Taxi games while you still can.
By
Nick Fernandez
•
June 17, 2025
•
0
•
Nick Fernandez / Android Authority
TL;DR
Nine retro SEGA games ported to mobile are now free without ads, but will lose support soon.
You can still download them, and they will likely remain in your account forever.
Free games include Crazy Taxi Classic, Shining Force Classics, Streets of Rage 2 Classic, and more.
SEGA has a long history of supporting its retro titles, with many ported directly to Android and iOS as part of the SEGA Forever program. However, the company will soon pull support for nearly its entire remaining catalog of mobile ports, including classic Sonic, Crazy Taxi, and Shining Force games.
There’s no telling how long they will remain on the Google Play Store, but the good news is that they’ve all been made free. Previously, most were paid titles costing roughly $2, or were playable for free with IAP to remove ads.
The announcement came not via any official channels, but rather via an in-game popup in the affected titles. It reads: “Support for this game will be discontinued, but you can continue playing offline! If you’d like to learn more about great SEGA games to play, please click the link below.” The link leads to the SEGA homepage.
This message implies that the game will still be playable after it’s removed from the Play Store, provided you have claimed it on your account. This was the case for previous SEGA Forever titles that were pulled a few years ago, which included games like Phantasy Star Classics and Vectorman Classic.
Unfortunately, it was only a matter of time before the rest of these games lost support. The SEGA Forever program was discontinued in late 2023, and the last port was added to Android way back in 2019. While the ports didn’t always live up to
emulation
, they did have
full controller support
, with many getting tens of millions of downloads.

data.title: Hurl: Run and test HTTP requests with plain text
data.author: flykespice
data.article_summary: Hurl是一个命令行工具，使用纯文本格式运行和测试HTTP请求。它可以发送链式请求、捕获值并评估响应的头部和主体。Hurl适用于获取数据和测试HTTP会话，支持HTML内容、REST/SOAP/GraphQL API以及其他基于XML/JSON的API。它允许对响应的状态码、头部、内容进行多种断言，并支持XPath、JSONPath等查询。Hurl还可以用于测试HTTP端点的性能和响应字节，并易于集成到CI/CD中，支持多种报告格式。Hurl使用libcurl作为底层HTTP引擎，具有快速、高效、支持IPv6和HTTP/3的特点。它采用单一可执行文件，易于安装和使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Hurl工具的使用体验、优缺点以及与其他工具的比较

不同观点：
• **支持观点：**
  - **[dm03514]**：认为Hurl在CI中用于执行HTTP请求测试非常有用，尤其是其具有测试套件模式和单独调用模式。尽管对配置语言有些不满意，但整体上非常有价值。Hurl帮助强化了接口和实现的分离，并且在LLM辅助开发中起到作用。
  - **[1a527dd5]**：从Runscope切换到Hurl后，解决了版本控制问题，可以清楚看到更改历史，非常满意。
  - **[perrygeo]**：在将一个Web服务从Python移植到Rust时，Hurl提供了独立于语言的集成测试，非常有用。并且Hurl与Rust的cargo测试工具集成良好。
  - **[manithree]**：认为Hurl可以很好地替代Postman，尤其是在Emacs编辑器中集成后，还创建了AWS Lambda监控工具。

• **中立/探索观点：**
  - **[hliyan]**：认为Hurl的文档示例部分很好，能够快速展示工具的价值，但对于工具的整体判断还需要进一步了解。
  - **[kalli]**：长期使用Vscode-restclient，最近转向了httpyac，正在考虑Hurl是否适合自己。指出不同工具在请求结果作为输入的语法上缺乏统一标准，导致工具间的兼容性问题。

• **质疑观点：**
  - **[3eb7988a1663]**：对Hurl的必要性提出质疑，认为如果使用Django等框架，内部测试工具已经足够，使用Hurl可能会增加额外工作，并失去调试便利性。认为除非是为了确保API的通用性，否则使用Hurl的理由不充分。
  - **[yoavm]**：对Hurl的响应状态代码断言位置设计不理解，认为应该放在`[Asserts]`部分，而不是请求部分。

• **工具比较观点：**
  - **[twodave]**：将Hurl与自己设计的HTTP测试工具Nap进行比较，认为如果需要快速并行运行大量测试，Nap可能也是一个选择。
  - **[chvid]**：提到Hurl与VS Code的REST客户端扩展类似，都是用于HTTP测试的工具。
  - **[a57721]**：提到在JVM项目中使用Karate进行集成测试，认为Karate提供了更灵活的JavaScript支持，用于构造请求和断言。

• **技术细节观点：**
  - **[the_arun]**：认为Hurl与IntelliJ中的HTTP客户端工具类似。
  - **[Thaxll]**：对Hurl的依赖和代码行数提出疑问，不确定1.5k行的CLI工具是否符合Rust开发的常规。

补充讨论：
- Hurl在不同语言和框架中的应用场景和优劣被广泛讨论，尤其是与Django内部测试工具、Karate等其他工具的比较。
- 工具间的语法不兼容问题被提出，尤其是在不同HTTP测试工具之间。
- 对Hurl的设计选择（如响应状态代码断言位置）存在一些疑惑和讨论。
- 不同用户根据自身需求和使用场景对Hurl的评价各异，有的非常满意，有的则持怀疑态度。

What's Hurl?
Hurl is a command line tool that runs
HTTP requests
defined in a simple
plain text format
.
It can chain requests, capture values and evaluate queries on headers and body response. Hurl is very
versatile: it can be used for both
fetching data
and
testing HTTP
sessions.
Hurl makes it easy to work with
HTML
content,
REST / SOAP / GraphQL
APIs, or any other
XML / JSON
based APIs.
# Go home and capture token
GET https://example.org
HTTP 200
[Captures]
csrf_token: xpath "string(//meta[@name='_csrf_token']/@content)"
# Do login!
POST https://example.org/login
X-CSRF-TOKEN: {{csrf_token}}
[Form]
user: toto
password: 1234
HTTP 302
Chaining multiple requests is easy:
GET https://example.org/api/health
GET https://example.org/api/step1
GET https://example.org/api/step2
GET https://example.org/api/step3
Also an HTTP Test Tool
Hurl can run HTTP requests but can also be used to
test HTTP responses
.
Different types of queries and predicates are supported, from
XPath
and
JSONPath
on body response,
to assert on status code and response headers.
It is well adapted for
REST / JSON APIs
POST https://example.org/api/tests
{
"id": "4568",
"evaluate": true
}
HTTP 200
[Asserts]
header "X-Frame-Options" == "SAMEORIGIN"
jsonpath "$.status" == "RUNNING"    # Check the status code
jsonpath "$.tests" count == 25      # Check the number of items
jsonpath "$.id" matches /\d{4}/     # Check the format of the id
HTML content
GET https://example.org
HTTP 200
[Asserts]
xpath "normalize-space(//head/title)" == "Hello world!"
GraphQL
POST https://example.org/graphql
```graphql
{
human(id: "1000") {
name
height(unit: FOOT)
}
}
```
HTTP 200
and even
SOAP APIs
POST https://example.org/InStock
Content-Type: application/soap+xml; charset=utf-8
SOAPAction: "http://www.w3.org/2003/05/soap-envelope"
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="http://www.w3.org/2003/05/soap-envelope" xmlns:m="https://example.org">
<soap:Header></soap:Header>
<soap:Body>
<m:GetStockPrice>
<m:StockName>GOOG</m:StockName>
</m:GetStockPrice>
</soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>
HTTP 200
Hurl can also be used to test the
performance
of HTTP endpoints
GET https://example.org/api/v1/pets
HTTP 200
[Asserts]
duration < 1000  # Duration in ms
And check response bytes
GET https://example.org/data.tar.gz
HTTP 200
[Asserts]
sha256 == hex,039058c6f2c0cb492c533b0a4d14ef77cc0f78abccced5287d84a1a2011cfb81;
Finally, Hurl is easy to
integrate in CI/CD
, with text, JUnit, TAP and HTML reports
Why Hurl?
Text Format:
for both devops and developers
Fast CLI:
a command line for local dev and continuous integration
Single Binary:
easy to install, with no runtime required
Powered by curl
Hurl is a lightweight binary written in
Rust
. Under the hood, Hurl HTTP engine is
powered by
libcurl
, one of the most powerful and reliable file transfer libraries.
With its text file format, Hurl adds syntactic sugar to run and test HTTP requests,
but it's still the
curl
that we love:
fast
,
efficient
and
IPv6 / HTTP/3 ready
.
Feedbacks
To support its development,
star Hurl on GitHub
!
Feedback, suggestion, bugs or improvements
are welcome.
POST https://hurl.dev/api/feedback
{
"name": "John Doe",
"feedback": "Hurl is awesome!"
}
HTTP 200

data.title: Behind the scenes: Redpanda Cloud's response to the GCP outage
data.author: eatonphil
data.article_summary: 2025年6月12日，Google Cloud Platform（GCP）由于API管理系统的自动化配额更新引发了全球性宕机，影响了大量互联网服务。然而，Redpanda Cloud的客户未受明显影响，归功于其专门设计的SLA和基于单元（cell-based）的架构。事件过程中，Redpanda Cloud的监控一度处于降级状态，但由于自托管的可观察性数据和堆栈，仍能评估影响。尽管第三方警报服务受影响，Redpanda团队通过其他手段监控系统，提前创建低严重性事件以协调应对潜在问题。在GCP确认问题并实施缓解措施后，Redpanda Cloud未发现客户受负面影响。此次事件展示了复杂系统中的“蝴蝶效应”以及安全和可靠性措施的重要性，如反馈控制、负载削减和回压应用等。尽管警报通知延迟，Redpanda Cloud通过主动联系客户和高错误率处理，成功维持了系统稳定。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：RedPanda在GCP大规模宕机事件中的表现及其架构设计

不同观点：
• RadiozRadioz：认为文章夸大了RedPanda的成就。虽然他们未受GCP宕机影响，但这主要是因为他们没有使用出问题的服务，且仅依赖第三方报警和监控系统。文章给人一种自夸的感觉，但实际上并没有展示出特别的应急处理或技术亮点，唯一提到的预防措施是超额配置磁盘空间，而这本应是常规操作。

• zzyzxd：批评文章过于冗长且自夸，指出RedPanda的架构并不完美。具体问题包括报警系统不耐用，宕机期间只能人工监控；存储使用超出正常水平且无异常检测和报警。此外，不理解为何要贬低Crowdstrike，认为这是不必要的。

• rybosome：同情GCP当前的处境，指出在大规模宕机事件中，GCP内部可能面临极大的压力和困难，特别是在已经因高可靠性要求而行动受限的情况下。

• diroussel：对文章中关于复杂系统和蝴蝶效应的描述提出异议，认为线性系统也可以是复杂的，并能表现出蝴蝶效应，而不仅仅是非线性系统。

• Peterpanzeri：批评RedPanda的声明，认为“我们的设计恰好没有使用到出问题的服务部分”是一种侥幸心态，希望他们下次能做好准备。

• raverbashing：对文章中将简单的架构原则称为“架构模式”感到有趣，认为这是把 obvious 的事情用复杂的语言表述出来，但认可其观点的正确性。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于RedPanda是否真的在此次宕机事件中展现了卓越的技术优势，还是仅仅因为侥幸未受影响。
• 对RedPanda架构设计和报警系统的耐用性、异常检测能力的质疑。
• 对文章中贬低其他公司（如Crowdstrike）的做法表示不解和不满。
• 对复杂系统和蝴蝶效应的技术性讨论，展示了读者对技术概念的不同理解。

What happened, how we handled it, and what we learned during the global GCP outage on June 12th
By

On Jun 12th, 2025, Google Cloud Platform (GCP) experienced an unfortunate global outage triggered by an automated quota update to their API management system.Â
What was a major outage for a large part of the internet was just another normal day for
Redpanda Cloud
customers. While GCP dealt with the widespread disruption that impacted many critical services, Redpanda Cloud clusters in GCP remained stable, thanks to being purposely designed for the
SLA we offer
, along with a
cell-based architecture
that we also made a
product principle
. But behind the scenes, it was far from quiet.
This post provides a brief timeline of events from our own experience, our response, previously untold details about Redpanda Cloud, and closing thoughts on safety and reliability practices in our industry.
Why do incidents like this happen
Modern computer systems are complex systems âÂ and complex systems are characterized by their non-linear nature, which means that observed changes in an output
are not
proportional to the change in the input. This concept is also known in chaos theory as the
butterfly effect
, or in systems thinking, with the expression, âThe whole is greater than the sum of its partsâ.Â
When this mathematical fact is acknowledged, safety and reliabiilty measures are put in place, such as closing feedback control loops, phasing change rollouts, shedding load, applying backpressure, randomizing retries, and defining incident response processes, among others.
GCPâs seemingly innocuous automated quota update triggered a
butterfly effect
that no human could have predicted, affecting several companies âÂ some known for their impressive engineering culture and considered internet pillars for their long-standing availability record.
The timeline
18:41:00 UTC
Our Google Cloud Technical Account Manager (TAM) notified us about the outage:
18:42:00 UTC
We began to assess the impact on our Redpanda Cloud GCP customers, including whether we had received any support tickets.Â
18:43:00 UTC
We noticed our monitoring was running in a degraded state. Despite self-hosting our observability data and stack, we still use a third-party provider for dashboarding and alerting needs. This provider was partially affected. We could still monitor metrics, but we were not getting alert notifications.Â
We deemed the loss of alert notifications not critical since we were still able to assess the impact through other means, such as querying our self-managed metrics and logging stack.
19:08:00 UTC
At this point, it was clear that multiple GCP services were experiencing a global outage, despite not having received support tickets from our customers or being paged by Redpanda Cloud alerts. So, in preparation for the worst, we preemptively created a low-severity incident to coordinate the response to multiple
potential
incidents.
19:23:00 UTC
We were notified by the vendor we use for managing cloud marketplaces that they were having issues. They were affected by the
Cloudflare outage
, which we later learned was connected to the GCP outage. Having this service degraded was not critical to us, so we put it on the waiting list.
19:41:00 UTC
Google identified the triggering cause and applied mitigations. At this point, there was no evidence that Redpanda Cloud customers were being negatively impacted.
20:26:00 UTC
We began receiving delayed alert notifications, mostly related to an increase in tiered storage errors, which is not Redpandaâs primary storage. We didnât get high disk utilization alerts, which we typically receive when the tiered storage subsystem has been experiencing issues for an extended period (days).
Additionally, as a reliability measure, we leave disk space unused and used-but-reclaimable (for caching), which we can reclaim if the situation warrants it. This outage was not that situation.
20:56:00 UTC
We proactively started reaching out to customers with the highest tiered storage error rates to ensure we were not missing anything, and also to show our support, as is customary. We fully manage these BYOC clusters on behalf of our customers and have complete visibility â we know the answers to the questions, but we ask anyway. These are complex systems, after all.
21:38:00 UTC
After closely monitoring our GCP fleet for some time, we considered the incident mitigatedâwith the severity unchanged (SEV4), and no evidence of negative customer impact. We noticed an increase in error rate for API calls against GCS, with minimal latency impact in some cases. However, hundreds of GCP clusters were up and healthy.

44338089.article_summary: 2025年6月12日，Google Cloud Platform（GCP）由于API管理系统的自动化配额更新引发了全球性宕机，影响了大量互联网服务。然而，Redpanda Cloud的客户未受明显影响，归功于其专门设计的SLA和基于单元（cell-based）的架构。事件过程中，Redpanda Cloud的监控一度处于降级状态，但由于自托管的可观察性数据和堆栈，仍能评估影响。尽管第三方警报服务受影响，Redpanda团队通过其他手段监控系统，提前创建低严重性事件以协调应对潜在问题。在GCP确认问题并实施缓解措施后，Redpanda Cloud未发现客户受负面影响。此次事件展示了复杂系统中的“蝴蝶效应”以及安全和可靠性措施的重要性，如反馈控制、负载削减和回压应用等。尽管警报通知延迟，Redpanda Cloud通过主动联系客户和高错误率处理，成功维持了系统稳定。
44338089.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：RedPanda在GCP大规模宕机事件中的表现及其架构设计

不同观点：
• RadiozRadioz：认为文章夸大了RedPanda的成就。虽然他们未受GCP宕机影响，但这主要是因为他们没有使用出问题的服务，且仅依赖第三方报警和监控系统。文章给人一种自夸的感觉，但实际上并没有展示出特别的应急处理或技术亮点，唯一提到的预防措施是超额配置磁盘空间，而这本应是常规操作。

• zzyzxd：批评文章过于冗长且自夸，指出RedPanda的架构并不完美。具体问题包括报警系统不耐用，宕机期间只能人工监控；存储使用超出正常水平且无异常检测和报警。此外，不理解为何要贬低Crowdstrike，认为这是不必要的。

• rybosome：同情GCP当前的处境，指出在大规模宕机事件中，GCP内部可能面临极大的压力和困难，特别是在已经因高可靠性要求而行动受限的情况下。

• diroussel：对文章中关于复杂系统和蝴蝶效应的描述提出异议，认为线性系统也可以是复杂的，并能表现出蝴蝶效应，而不仅仅是非线性系统。

• Peterpanzeri：批评RedPanda的声明，认为“我们的设计恰好没有使用到出问题的服务部分”是一种侥幸心态，希望他们下次能做好准备。

• raverbashing：对文章中将简单的架构原则称为“架构模式”感到有趣，认为这是把 obvious 的事情用复杂的语言表述出来，但认可其观点的正确性。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于RedPanda是否真的在此次宕机事件中展现了卓越的技术优势，还是仅仅因为侥幸未受影响。
• 对RedPanda架构设计和报警系统的耐用性、异常检测能力的质疑。
• 对文章中贬低其他公司（如Crowdstrike）的做法表示不解和不满。
• 对复杂系统和蝴蝶效应的技术性讨论，展示了读者对技术概念的不同理解。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI代理应用在浏览Hacker News（HN）等网站时的实用性及功能价值

不同观点：
• soared认为整个早上花在HN上并非明智之举，且质疑AI代理帮助阅读HN的必要性。他表示不理解该应用的使用场景，觉得只是简单地提供图片和摘要，并没有实际用途。后续补充提到，这个应用似乎每季度发布一次，且发布内容单一，进一步质疑其价值。

• ukuina分享了自己创建的免费网站HackYourNews.com，该网站使用Gemini Flash技术，不仅能总结HN文章，还能总结HN评论。ukuina的观点是，这样的工具确实有其价值，特别是在信息过载的情况下可以帮助用户快速获取关键信息。

• Y_Y以讽刺的口吻提出，一个能够挑选最佳创意、执行并最终破产的AI代理，虽然能提供总结和学习经验，但认为单靠总结无法带来成功。他质疑过度依赖AI总结工具可能会导致思维僵化，失去独立思考的机会。

• donclark表示对“记忆搜索”功能感兴趣，认为将新信息与之前看过的内容关联起来是非常有用的功能，这可能帮助用户更好地整合和理解信息。

• ClawsOnPaws简单提到该应用在其所在地区不可用，暗示可能存在地域限制问题，影响用户体验。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及AI代理应用的实用性、功能创新以及其潜在的局限性。
• 部分用户对AI代理工具的价值持怀疑态度，认为过度依赖可能会适得其反，而其他用户则认为这些工具在信息过载的情况下确实能提供帮助。
• 地域限制问题也被提及，显示出用户体验中可能存在的障碍。

data.title: Fundamental Problems of Lisp, the Cons Cell (2024)
data.author: gudzpoz
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了LISP语言中的一个基本问题：cons单元用于构建列表的局限性。LISP的核心是基于函数式编程和列表操作，但其列表结构依赖于硬件概念的cons单元，导致每个列表节点只能包含两个元素。若要构建更长的列表，必须嵌套cons单元并采用特殊解释方式，称为“适当列表”。这种设计限制了列表处理的发展，使得操作复杂且不统一。文章建议通过标准化适当列表和隐藏低级cons操作来改进LISP。同时，作者批评了cons及其相关函数（如car、cdr等）导致代码不一致和复杂性，并以假设语言gisp中的三元单元fons为例，说明了类似问题。最后，文章探讨了LISP的cons问题为何未被解决，归因于历史和技术限制。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Lisp中的cons细胞和其相关的高阶抽象问题

不同观点：
• noosphr认为Lisp的核心不是函数式编程语言，且cons细胞在深层嵌套结构中并不常用。他指出，虽然Lisp可以操作抽象语法树，但在实际使用中，嵌套列表的复杂操作非常少见。
• lisper为cons细胞辩护，认为其问题并非源于cons细胞本身，而是由于对其不当的使用。他将cons细胞与C语言中的指针进行对比，指出两者在滥用时都会导致问题，但其本身并非缺陷。
• smarks指出，Xah Lee的观点早在1998年就已存在，并认为其问题具有误导性，质疑cons细胞的必要性实际上是在贬低前人的智慧。
• DonaldFisk强调，cons细胞是Lisp不可或缺的一部分，类似于Smalltalk中的对象或APL中的数组，是Lisp语言的重要组成部分。
• alphazard认为cons细胞的间接机制与其连接机制混淆，建议引入不同的内存管理方法以实现更高效的数据结构。
• behnamoh推荐Janet语言，认为其解决了cons细胞的问题，但其文档不够完善。
• Jtsummers引用LISP I手册，指出cons、car和cdr是用于创建和操作S表达式，而非仅限于列表，强调其自语言创始以来的核心地位。
• dragontamer认为cons细胞作为基础数据结构具有强大功能，但现代高性能编程可能需要更多基于数组的结构。
• chubot提出Clojure中cons细胞使用较少，因为其基于不可变的maps和vectors，质疑cons细胞在现代Lisp变种中的必要性。
• kazinator展示了TXR Lisp中对car/cdr的扩展使用，显示cons细胞在不同实现中的灵活性。

补充讨论：
• 关于Xah Lee的个人背景及其在Lisp社区中的争议性 reputation，部分评论者对其观点持怀疑态度。
• 评论中多次提及Lisp的早期历史及其与其他语言（如C、Smalltalk、Haskell）在数据结构和编程范式上的对比。
• 对于cons细胞在现代计算机体系结构中的性能问题也有讨论，尤其是与内存查找相关的延迟问题。

争议的焦点：
• Cons细胞是否是Lisp中必要且高效的基本结构，或者是否应被更现代的数据结构替代。
• Xah Lee对cons细胞的批评是否成立，部分评论者认为其观点带有偏见和误解。

44310996.article_content:
Fundamental Problems of LISP, the Cons Cell
By Xah Lee. Date:
2024-07-02
.
(this essay is originally written around 2008)
The Cons Business
The other fundamental problem in the language is its cons cells as its list construction primitive.
Lisp at core is based on functional programing on lists.
This is a powerful paradigm.
However, for historical reasons, lisp's list is based on the hardware concept of âconsâ cell.
From a mathematical, functional, API point of view, what this means is that lisp's âlistâ is limited to a max of 2 elements.
If you want a longer list, you must nest it and interpret it in a special way.
(i.e.
effectively creating a mini-protocol, known as âproper listâ.)
The cons fundamentally crippled the development of list processing.
Lisp being historically based the cons for about 4 decades. The cons and the associated {car cdr cadr caadr caddr caaar cdddr â¦} are fundamentally rooted in the lisp langs, is thus not something that can be easily mended. This is unfortunate. However, this situation could be improved.  By, for example:
Create a standard that all list data structures must be proper lists. (this would also mean re-implement association lists to be based on proper lists)
Expose only higher-level list manipulation functions (i.e. interfaces to cons) in all new literature.
Even mark cons related constructs as obsolete.
One of the myth that is quickly injected into budding lispers, is that cons is powerful. It is powerful in the sense assembly lang is powerful.
Lisp's cons is perhaps the greatest fuck up in the history of computer languages.
Racket Lisp described the cons problem well:
Racket Doc on Lisp Cons Problem
For some concrete examples of problems caused by the cons, see:
Guy Steele Says: Don't Iterate, Recurse, and Get rid of lisp cons!
Why Lisp Not Have a Generic Copy-List Function?
Lisp List Problem
Frequently Asked Questions
If you don't like cons, lisp has arrays and hashmaps, too.
Suppose there's a lang called gisp.
In gisp, there's cons but also fons.
Fons is just like cons except it has 3 cells with 3 accessors: car, cbr, cdr.
Now, gisp is a old lang, the fons are deeply rooted in the lang.
Every some 100 lines of code you'll see a use of fons with its extra accessor cbr, or any one of the cbaar, cdabr, cbbar, cbbbar, etc.
You got annoyed by this.
You complain that fons is bad.
But then some gisp fanatics retorts: âIf you don't like fons, gisp has cons, too!â.
You see, by âhaving something tooâ, does not solve the problem of pollution.
I like the cons concept. Even in functional languages like Haskell it is popular, for example, when matching in the form of (x:xs), which is the same like car/cdr in Lisp.
Languages that have a list data type implemented as linked list, with First, Rest accessors, do not expose it as API in the same way lisp does with explicit cons.
Lisp's cons forces programer to think of list in a low-level nested of 2-item construction, with explicit functions like âcddrâ, âcadaarâ etc, and even a special notation â(A .
B)â.
This hinders the development tree functions.
For example, one might write a function that extracts the leafs of a binary tree.
But due to cons, there is no single data structure to implement a binary tree.
You can have the whole structure made of cons, or cons only for ending branches, or whole structure made of âproper listâ.
Consequently, what's considered a leaf depends on your implementation, and the code to traverse the tree also depends on how you used cons.
Worse, any proper list can have improper list as elements.
So, you can have a list of cons, or cons of lists, cons of cons, list of lists, or any mix.
The overall effect of the cons is that it prevents lisp to have a uniform high level treatment of lists, with the result that development of functions that work on tree are inconsistent and few.
2009-07-21 Addendum : there was actually a lang with âfonsâ of 3 cells. {Haines, E.
C., The TREET List Processing Language.
M.S.
Thesis, MIT, Cambridge, Mass., August 1964.
Also SR-133, The MITRE Corporation, Bedford, Mass., April 1965.} Thanks to
Richard Fateman
for alerting me to this.
Why Lisp's Cons Problem Never Got Fixed?
Now, a little speculation.
We might wonder, why lisp has the cons problem and was never addressed in Common Lisp or Scheme Lisp?
Historical Necessity
I guess at the time, 1960s and 1970s, the very fact that you could have a concept like a list in a lang and manipulate it as a unit, is a very advanced concept.
The list, being built up by hardware cons, is just something that is necessary for implementation for practical considerations.
(think for a moment what computers are like in the 1960s.)
Having data as a single manipulable object (list) didn't really become popular until the 1990s.
(notably due to Perl) And today, it is THE most important feature of high-level languages.
(e.g. Perl Python Ruby PHP JavaScript)
Deep Nesting is Rare

data.title: Record DDoS pummels site with once-unimaginable 7.3Tbps of junk traffic
data.author: Brajeshwar
data.article_summary: 文章主要报道了一次创纪录的DDoS攻击，其流量达到7.3Tbps，针对Cloudflare的一名客户。攻击者使用了“地毯式轰炸”策略，向单个IP地址的多个端口发送大量垃圾数据，其中大部分通过UDP协议传输。UDP洪水攻击通过发送高量数据包使目标服务器过载。此外，攻击还利用了反射攻击技术，借助中间服务器放大攻击效果。此次攻击还涉及Mirai僵尸网络，由被入侵的物联网设备组成。DDoS攻击规模在过去几十年中不断增大，显示出网络安全面临的持续威胁。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Cloudflare宣称阻止大规模网络攻击的可信度及技术细节

不同观点：
• smokel认为这次攻击并没有特别复杂，认为只是通过一个简单的for-loop（循环）就可以实现，暗示攻击的技术含量不高。
• ksec则关注用户体验问题，特别是当Cloudflare的验证码（captcha）不工作时，用户（尤其是在特定设备和浏览器上）该如何应对，提出了替代方案的需求。
• esafak提出了关于攻击者身份和动机的问题，质疑谁在发动攻击以及他们的目的。
• encom强烈质疑Cloudflare的可信度，认为这篇文章像是一篇赞助广告，缺乏可验证的细节，并对Ars Technica发布这样的内容表示失望。

补充讨论：
• ChrisArchitect提到在另一个讨论平台（Hacker News）上有重复的讨论，并提供了链接供参考。
• balanc质疑Cloudflare是否有动机夸大其成功阻止的攻击规模，指出Cloudflare可能有经济利益驱动，并预先反驳了可能的反驳意见。

争议焦点：
• Cloudflare宣称阻止的攻击规模是否真实，是否存在夸大其词的情况。
• 对Cloudflare的整体可信度及媒体报道的真实性存在广泛质疑。

Large-scale attacks designed to bring down Internet services by sending them more traffic than they can process keep getting bigger, with the largest one yet, measured at 7.3 terabits per second, being reported Friday by Internet security and performance provider Cloudflare.
The 7.3Tbps attack amounted to 37.4 terabytes of junk traffic that hit the target in just 45 seconds. That's an almost incomprehensible amount of data, equivalent to more than 9,300 full-length HD movies or 7,500 hours of HD streaming content in well under a minute.
Indiscriminate target bombing
Cloudflare
said
the attackers “carpet bombed” an average of nearly 22,000 destination ports of a single IP address belonging to the target, identified only as a Cloudflare customer. A total of 34,500 ports were targeted, indicating the thoroughness and well-engineered nature of the attack.
The vast majority of the attack was delivered in the form of User Datagram Protocol packets. Legitimate UDP-based transmissions are used in especially time-sensitive communications, such as those for video playback, gaming applications, and DNS lookups. It speeds up communications by not formally establishing a connection before data is transferred. Unlike the more common Transmission Control Protocol, UDP doesn't wait for a connection between two computers to be established through a handshake and doesn't check whether data is properly received by the other party. Instead, it immediately sends data from one machine to another.
UDP flood attacks send extremely high volumes of packets to random or specific ports on the target IP. Such floods can saturate the target’s Internet link or overwhelm internal resources with more packets than they can handle.
Since UDP doesn't require a handshake, attackers can use it to flood a targeted server with torrents of traffic without first obtaining the server's permission to begin the transmission. UDP floods typically send large numbers of datagrams to multiple ports on the target system. The target system, in turn, must send an equal number of data packets back to indicate the ports aren't reachable. Eventually, the target system buckles under the strain, resulting in legitimate traffic being denied.
A much smaller portion of the attack, measured at just 0.004 percent, was delivered as reflection attacks. Reflection attacks direct malicious traffic to one or more third-party intermediaries, such as Network Time Protocol services for syncing server clocks. The attacker spoofs the sender IP of the malicious packets to give the appearance they’re being delivered by the final target. When the third party sends a response, it's delivered to the target rather than the destination of the original source of the traffic.
Reflection attacks provide multiple benefits to attackers. For one, such attacks cause the DDoS to be delivered from a wide variety of destinations. That makes it harder for targets to defend against the onslaught. Additionally, by choosing intermediary servers known to generate responses that are in some cases thousands of times bigger than the originating request, attackers can magnify the firepower available to them by a thousandfold or more. Cloudflare and other players routinely advise server administrators to lock down servers to prevent them from responding to spoofed packets, but inevitably, many don't heed the advice.
Cloudflare said the record DDoS exploited various reflection or amplification vectors, including the previously mentioned Network Time Protocol; the Quote of the Day Protocol, which listens on UDP port 17 and responds with a short quote or message; the Echo Protocol, which responds with the same data it receives; and Portmapper services used identify resources available to applications connecting through the Remote Procedure Call.
Cloudflare said the attack was also delivered through one or more Mirai-based botnets. Such botnets are typically made up of home and small office routers, web cameras, and other Internet of Things devices that have been compromised.
DDoS sizes have continued a steady climb over the past three decades. In
March
, Nokia reported that a botnet dubbed Eleven11bot delivered a DOS with a peak of 6.5Tbps. In May, KrebsonSecurity
said
it came under a DDos that peaked at 6.3Tbps.

data.title: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Fuzzing for Porting Programs
data.author: dlwh
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了利用大型语言模型（LLM）自动化将C语言程序移植到Rust的潜力，特别是通过模糊测试和拓扑排序构建移植策略的有效性。作者反思了LLM生成代码的趋势，预测未来计算机将生成大部分代码，从而改变库维护和API管理的方式。LLM可以帮助解决API不一致问题，甚至可以自动迁移到新版本，从而简化大规模重构。文章还以TensorFlow为例，说明维护大型技术债务项目所面临的挑战，并提出通过LLM降低复杂重构成本的可能性。这为未来代码维护和库改进提供了新的思路。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕自动翻译软件的有效性和实际应用的讨论

不同观点：
• [bgwalter] 认为在当前系统中，虽然可以引入人工来解决问题，但翻译软件的输出质量非常差，修复这些翻译比直接人工翻译耗费更多时间。他还指出，虽然文章提到被翻译的软件相对简单，但没有证据表明这种翻译不会改变软件的行为，因此该技术是否适用于更广泛的场景仍存疑。

• [highpost] 没有直接发表观点，但指出了该评论主题在其他平台上已有讨论，并提供了一个链接（可能意在引导读者参考更多信息）。

• [james_marks] 更关注性能问题，特别是C语言版本与新的Rust版本之间的性能对比，质疑新版本的性能是否有显著提升，尤其是在之前Rust版本存在性能问题的情况下。

• [dan_can_code] 提出了一个技术性问题，即相关网站无法访问，可能影响了对讨论主题的进一步探讨或验证。

补充讨论：
• 翻译软件的质量和其在实际应用中的可行性是主要争议点，尤其是翻译是否会改变软件行为以及人工修复的成本问题。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是不同编程语言版本之间的性能差异，特别是Rust版本的性能是否得到了改善。
• 网站宕机问题也对讨论的连续性造成了影响，读者可能无法获取更多背景信息或进一步的技术细节。

44307275.article_content:
The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Fuzzing for Porting Programs
A simple strategy of having LLMs write fuzz tests and build up a port in topological order seems effective at automating porting from C to Rust.
Agents are starting to produce more and more code
A week or 2 back, I was reflecting on some code Claude had generated for me and
I had a sort of moment of clarity. "Clarity" might be overstating it; more
like the type of thought you have in the shower or after a few beers. Anyway.
The thought was: LLMs produce more and more code, and they'll eventually be
producing more code than people. We can imagine at some point we're going to
fork from mostly people writing code to mostly computers. What does this mean
for how we're going to treat our libraries and code maintenance in the future?
LLMs make it easier to deal with API issues or inconsistencies, they're dealing
with it, not us. Will this continue, leaving us with a
The
Princess and the Pea
situation where we deal with piles of leaking
abstractions? Or will we use LLMs to radically change our APIs when needed - will
things get cleaner and better and faster as we go?
LLMs open up the door to performing radical updates that we'd
never really consider in the past. We can port our libraries from one language
to another. We can change our APIs to fix issues, and give downstream users an
LLM prompt to migrate over to the new version automatically, instead of
rewriting their code themselves. We can make massive internal refactorings.
These are types of tasks that in the past,
rightly
, a senior engineer would
reject in a project until its the last possibly option. Breaking customers
almost never pays off, and its hard to justify refactoring on a "maintenance
mode" project.
But if its more about finding the right prompt and letting an
LLM do the work, maybe that changes our decision process.
Maintaining big important libraries is no fun
I used to work on
TensorFlow
. (TensorFlow is a system to develop
gradient based models, like PyTorch. It's not used so much anymore outside of
Google.) Now TensorFlow had some design flaws in the core language, and a
botched version 1 -> version 2 migration didn't help matters too much. But as a
maintainer, the biggest issue was the enormous technical debt. It suffered from
a sort of "career advancement syndrome"
I sadly missed this period and only was around for the aftermath where we had to deal with the cruft.
: TensorFlow was popular and you got credit for
contributing to it, so there was a huge incentive to add some feature as quickly
as you could and then get away.
As a result of a few years of this style of development, a huge surface of
Python code had been cobbled together on top of the C++ core. The complexity
only spiraled over time: engineers came into the project and needed to get
something done. Increasingly the easiest thing to do was to add some Python global or
context manager, shove something in it, then grab it later. Do this over and
over and eventually it becomes impossibly to figure out what's happening. It
also ended up being incredibly slow. It would take 10s of minutes to build some
graphs (TensorFlow's equivalent of a program).
As a result of this over time TensorFlow became harder and harder to maintain,
much less evolve
It was also hard to keep good engineers working on the project. If
you're a good engineer, other teams want you and you could choose to work on
less crufty, more exciting projects like
Jax
or
XLA
, or you know, Ads.
. One idea we discussed internally to try to fix this was
porting the Python code, bit by bit, into a more comprehensible C++ layer, and
then re-exporting it via PyBind. At first you'd still call everything through
the Python interface, but as you ported code over, you could start to use the
internal C++ interfaces more and more, getting faster and more stable as you
went. This would incrementally improve the performance and consistency of the
system, or that was the hope.
But it would have been an enormous effort to do this all. Each time you tried to
port a module you'd reveal subtle errors or assumptions that you'd need to debug
and revisit, update users etc. Given our staffing, we couldn't really justify
the time versus the real work of making sure Ads didn't break.
Even though TensorFlow was moving to maintenance mode, if we could have made
this type of change it would have improved the maintainer and users' experience
for the years we need to keep the lights on. But because the cleanup was thorny
and slow, we just couldn't justify the cost.
This is by no means limited to TensorFlow. If you're working on something like
libexpat
its hard to justify
refactoring your code or rewriting it in Rust, no matter how potentially useful
it would be, when you've got this at the top of your page:
But what if we could make this type of refactoring much, much cheaper?

Claude
Code

data.author: blinding-streak

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：欧洲是否应减少对美国技术和政治支持的依赖，以及微软在此次事件中的角色和责任。

不同观点：
• bigtones和gentle认为，此次事件为欧洲提供了明确的证据，表明欧洲应减少对美国的依赖，发展自己的技术和基础设施，以保护自身利益。bigtones还以澳大利亚的立场为例，认为澳大利亚也应该这样做。

• NewJazz和decide1000对微软的反应表示不满。NewJazz批评微软没有抵抗或上诉美国的命令，显示其软弱和顺从。decide1000则认为，微软的行动破坏了欧美之间长期以来的关系，欧洲人将加速与美国的分离。

• nickdothutton提到，欧洲曾有计划建立自己的技术和基础设施，但未付诸实施。这表明欧洲有想法但缺乏行动力。

• shswkna认为，愤怒的对象应该是欧洲自身，而不是微软或美国。shswkna批评欧洲人活在幻想中，需要觉醒。

• creatonez将微软的行为与历史上其他科技公司参与战争罪行的例子相提并论，认为微软在当前的国际冲突中扮演了不光彩的角色。

• fuzzy2和buyucu关注技术细节，fuzzy2询问被关闭账户的类型，buyucu则表示因类似事件其公司将永远不会使用微软的产品。

• timsh虽然不试图为微软辩护，但建议像事件中的个人应使用更安全的通信工具，如ProtonMail，以保护其活动相关的通信。

• dudeinjapan分享了个人经历，提到微软曾在未警告的情况下暂停其电子邮件账户，认为此次事件属于更大、更险恶模式的一部分。

• yahoozoo将事件归因于以色列，暗示以色列在背后的影响。

补充讨论：
• 评论中多次提到欧洲应加强技术和基础设施的自主性，以减少对美国的依赖。
• 微软的顺从态度引发了对其责任和角色的广泛批评，部分评论者认为其在国际政治中扮演了不光彩的角色。
• 个人和企业对微软产品的信任度下降，部分评论者表示将考虑使用其他更安全的工具和服务。

data.title: Astronomers locate universe's 'missing' matter in the largest cosmic structures
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 天文学家发现了一条巨大的炽热气体丝状结构，连接四个星系团，长达2300万光年，质量为银河系的10倍。这一发现解释了宇宙中长期缺失的“普通物质”位置，这些物质以原子形式存在，构成了星星、行星等。此前，宇宙模型预测这些缺失的物质存在于连接密集星系团的丝状气体中，但因其暗淡且被其他光源掩盖，难以观测。通过XMM-Newton和Suzaku太空望远镜，天文学家首次清晰观测到这一结构，验证了宇宙模型的准确性，并有助于理解宇宙网（Cosmic Web）及宇宙大规模结构的形成。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：宇宙中“失踪气体”（missing baryons）问题以及其与暗物质理论的关系。

不同观点：
• [mosesbp的观点] 认为该研究仅分析了相对宇宙整体较小区域内的星系间气体（特别是WHIM），并指出作者自己也承认需要更多高质量的数据才能得出更确凿的结论。同时提到失踪气体问题是一个长期存在的难题，并引用多篇文献说明近年来有研究利用快速射电暴（Fast Radio Burst）数据尝试解决该问题，暗示气体存在于WHIM中可能是失踪气体的合理解释。
  
• [exegete的观点] 提出疑问，是否这意味着理论上的暗物质数量减少，因为暗物质的存在是为了解释观测到的引力效应，这些效应表明宇宙中应该存在比我们实际观测到的更多物质。这暗示了对失踪气体的解释可能会影响到暗物质理论的有效性。

补充讨论：
• [失踪气体的背景] mosesbp指出失踪气体问题主要集中在宇宙相对“近期”的历史中，并提到已有文献讨论了这一问题，强调了失踪气体和存在于星系间的气体（WHIM）之间的关联。
  
• [暗物质与失踪气体的关系] exegete的评论引发了关于失踪气体和暗物质之间关系的讨论。暗物质被认为是为了解释观测到的引力效应而假设的存在，而失踪气体问题则涉及普通物质的分布，二者虽然都涉及宇宙中的物质不足问题，但本质上属于不同的问题领域。

争议焦点：失踪气体的发现是否会减少对暗物质的需求，或二者是否存在相互影响。这涉及到宇宙学中对不同形式物质的理解和解释。

44338001.article_content:
An illustration of the cosmic web where the universe's missing matter was discovered
(Image credit: ESA/XMM-Newton and ISAS/JAXA.)
Astronomers have discovered a vast tendril of hot gas linking four galaxy clusters and stretching out for 23 million light-years, 230 times the length of our galaxy. With 10 times the mass of the Milky Way, this filamentary structure accounts for much of the universe's "missing matter," the search for which has baffled scientists for decades.
This "missing matter"
doesn't
refer to
dark matter
, the mysterious stuff that remains effectively invisible because it doesn't interact with light (sadly, that remains an ongoing puzzle). Instead, it is "ordinary matter" made up of atoms, composed of
electrons
,
protons
, and
neutrons
(collectively called
baryons
) which make up stars, planets, moons, and our bodies.
For decades, our best models of the universe have suggested that a third of the baryonic matter that should be out there in the cosmos is missing. This discovery of that missing matter suggests our best models of the universe were right all along. It could also reveal more about the "
Cosmic Web,
" the vast structure along which entire galaxies grew and gathered during the earlier epochs of our
13.8 billion-year-old universe.
The aforementioned models of the cosmos, including the
standard model of cosmology
, have long posited the idea that the missing baryonic matter of the universe is locked up in vast filaments of gas stretching between the densest pockets of space.
You may like
Astronomers discover dark matter 'bridge' linking colliding galaxies: 'This is the missing piece we've been looking for.'
Scientists find universe's missing matter while watching fast radio bursts shine through 'cosmic fog'
Gamma-ray bursts reveal largest structure in the universe is bigger and closer to Earth than we knew: 'The jury is still out on what it all means.'
Though astronomers have seen these filaments before, the fact that they are faint has meant that their light has been washed out by other sources like galaxies and
supermassive black hole
-powered
quasars
. That means the characteristics of these filaments have remained elusive.
But now, a team of astronomers has for the first time been able to determine the properties of one of these filaments, which links four galactic clusters in the local universe. These four clusters are all part of the
Shapley Supercluster
, a gathering of over 8,000 galaxies forming one of the most massive structures in the nearby cosmos.
"For the first time, our results closely match what we see in our leading model of the cosmos – something that's not happened before," team leader Konstantinos Migkas of Leiden Observatory in the Netherlands said in a statement. "It seems that the simulations were right all along."
Missing matter is hot stuff
The newly observed filament isn't just extraordinary in terms of its mass and size; it also has a temperature of a staggering 18 million degrees Fahrenheit (10 million degrees Celsius). That's around 1,800 times hotter than the
surface of the sun.

The filament stretches diagonally through the Shapely Supercluster.
Missing baryonic matter discovered by the XMM-Newton and Suzaku X-ray space telescopes
(Image credit: ESA/XMM-Newton and ISAS/JAXA. Acknowledgement: Migkas et al. (2025), ATG Europe)
Vital to the characterization of this filament was X-ray data from
XMM-Newton
and
Suzaku
, which made a great tag-team of telescopes.
While Suzaku, a
Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency
(JAXA) satellite, mapped X-ray light over a vast region of space, the
European Space Agency
(ESA) operated XMM-Newton zoomed in of X-ray points from supermassive black holes studded within the filament, "contaminating" it.
"Thanks to XMM-Newton, we could identify and remove these cosmic contaminants, so we knew we were looking at the gas in the filament and nothing else," team member and University of Bonn researcher Florian Pacaud said. "Our approach was really successful, and reveals that the filament is exactly as we'd expect from our best
large-scale simulations of the universe
."
The team then combined these X-ray observations with optical data from a plethora of other telescopes.
The core of the Shapley Supercluster, the largest cosmic structure in the local universe.
(Image credit: ESA & Planck Collaboration / Rosat/ Digitised Sky Survey)
Revealing this hitherto undiscovered tendril of hot matter connecting galaxy clusters has the potential to aid scientists' understanding of these extreme structures and how they are connected across
vast cosmic distances.
This could, in turn, aid our understanding of the Cosmic Web, filaments of matter that acted as a cosmic scaffold helping the universe to assemble in it

data.title: Your Hotel Is Bleeding $50k/year
data.author: dtw45
data.article_summary: 文章指出，许多酒店在不知情的情况下，每年在所谓“强制性”但实际上并非必须的IT服务上浪费大量资金。作者以自身经历为例，发现其酒店在三年内为一条多余的备份互联网线路支付了10.8万美元。通过审查，作者消除了这一不必要的支出，实现了每年3.6万美元的节省。文章列举了酒店常面临的六种资金浪费情况，包括自动续订陷阱、高级许可证骗局、彩色打印浪费、被遗忘的订阅、未申请的SLA返款以及过时技术的高维护成本。作者强调，酒店经理因忙碌而无法详细审查每一项IT支出，同时可能缺乏技术知识来质疑供应商的建议，导致不必要的开支。文章建议酒店管理者应更仔细地审查IT预算，以避免不必要的浪费并提高利润。

44336394.article_content:
June 21, 2025
•
5 min read

Cost Optimization
Your Hotel Is Bleeding $50,000+ Per Year on "Mandatory" IT Services
That Aren't Mandatory
And your vendors are counting on you never finding out
DW
Daniel T. Wolela
Former Multi-Property IT Director & EMEA Security Leader,
Marriott International
I walked into my new hotel property in Dubai in 2022 and
discovered something that made my stomach drop.
For three years, the hotel had been paying $3,000 per month for a
"mandatory" backup internet line. $108,000 in total waste. The
kicker? The hotel already had multiple ADSL lines providing perfect
redundancy.
When I questioned why we needed this expensive redundancy, I
discovered my predecessor had been told it was "mandatory" by
corporate. But when I dug deeper, there was no written policy
requiring it. No documentation. No justification.
I eliminated the redundant line immediately. $36,000 in annual
savings with zero impact on operations.
There was nothing mandatory about it. Just a $108,000 assumption
that nobody bothered to challenge.
If you're a hotel General Manager, this story should terrify
you.
Because right now, as you read this, your property is likely
hemorrhaging money on IT services you don't need, software you don't
use, and contracts you've never properly reviewed.
The Uncomfortable Truth About Hotel IT Spending
After conducting security audits across 450+ hotels in three
continents and personally managing IT operations for multiple
properties simultaneously (including opening 7 new hotels from
scratch), I can tell you this with certainty:
The average hotel wastes 20-30% of its IT budget on unnecessary
services.
That's not a typo. Nearly one-third of every dollar you spend on
technology is pure waste.
For a typical 150-room hotel spending $80,000 annually on IT, that's
$16,000-$24,000 bleeding out every year. Money that should flow to
your bottom line instead flows to vendors who've mastered the art of
selling you things you don't need.
The Six Ways Your Hotel Is Being Quietly Robbed
1. The Auto-Renewal Trap
Your property management system includes 12 modules. You use 3.
But you're paying for all 12 because nobody ever audited what
you actually need. Those unused modules auto-renew every year,
charging you thousands for features that benefit nobody except
your vendor's profit margins.
2. The Premium License Scam
Your front desk staff has "premium" software licenses with
advanced features they'll never touch. You're paying enterprise
rates for basic users. It's like buying first-class tickets for
passengers who only need coach.
3. The Color Printing Money Pit
Walk to any printer in your hotel right now. Check the settings.
I guarantee it's set to color by default. Your staff prints
everything in color—internal memos, shift schedules, maintenance
reports. You're paying premium rates to make black-and-white
documents slightly more colorful and infinitely more expensive.
4. The Forgotten Subscription Graveyard
In your accounting system right now are dozens of monthly
subscriptions you forgot existed. Software trials that became
paid subscriptions. Services purchased by former employees. Apps
that seemed useful once but haven't been opened in months. Each
one automatically renewing, quietly draining your budget.
5. The SLA Rebate You Never Claim
Your internet went down for 4 hours last month. Your PMS crashed
during check-in rush. Your phone system failed during a busy
weekend. Each outage violated your service level agreement. Each
violation entitles you to rebates. But you never claim them
because nobody told you they exist.
6. The "If It Ain't Broke, Don't Fix It" Money Trap
Your hotel is still using the same phone system from 2018. The
same internet package from 2019. The same security software from
2020. When did you last ask: "Is there something better
available now?"
Technology moves fast. What was cutting-edge six years ago is
now overpriced legacy equipment. That "premium" internet package
you've been auto-renewing? There's probably a faster, cheaper
option available today. Your ancient phone system that costs
$800/month in maintenance? Modern cloud-based systems deliver
better features for $200/month.
Why Smart Hotel Managers Fall for These Traps
You're not stupid. You're busy.
While you're managing guest complaints, staff schedules, and revenue
optimization, your IT vendors are optimizing something else:
extracting maximum profit from your property with minimum scrutiny.
They count on three things:
You're too busy to audit every line item
in your
IT budget
You lack the technical knowledge
to challenge
their recommendations
You're afraid to touch anything that "works"
even
if it's overpriced
This isn't your fault. You were hired to maximize guest satisfaction
and revenue, not become an IT procurement expert. But ignoring this
problem costs you real money. Money that could fund marketing
campaigns, property improvements, or simply improve your profit
margins.

data.title: MIT student prints AI polymer masks to restore paintings in hours
data.author: Brajeshwar
data.article_summary: MIT研究生Alex Kachkine开发了一种利用AI生成聚合物膜的技术，可以在数小时内修复受损的绘画，而传统方法需要数月甚至数年。该方法通过打印透明“面具”覆盖画作受损区域，面具包含精确匹配颜色的区域，且可逆，不永久改变原作。此技术利用计算机视觉和定制软件分析图像并生成修复方案，通过高精度喷墨打印机制作面具，应用保护级别的清漆固定，且未来可轻松移除。该方法特别适用于因受损而无法展出的艺术作品，有助于解决修复积压问题，同时保留详细的修复记录供未来参考。尽管如此，人类判断仍不可或缺，以确保修复符合伦理和艺术家的原意。研究发表于《Nature》。

MIT graduate student Alex Kachkine once spent nine months meticulously restoring a damaged baroque Italian painting, which left him plenty of time to wonder if technology could speed things up. Last week, MIT News
announced
his solution: a technique that uses AI-generated polymer films to physically restore damaged paintings in hours rather than months. The research
appears
in Nature.
Kachkine's method works by printing a transparent "mask" containing thousands of precisely color-matched regions that conservators can apply directly to an original artwork. Unlike traditional restoration, which permanently alters the painting, these masks can reportedly be removed whenever needed. So it's a reversible process that does not permanently change a painting.
"Because there's a digital record of what mask was used, in 100 years, the next time someone is working with this, they'll have an extremely clear understanding of what was done to the painting," Kachkine told MIT News. "And that's never really been possible in conservation before."
Figure 1 from the paper.
Credit:
MIT
Nature
reports
that up to 70 percent of institutional art collections remain hidden from public view due to damage—a large amount of cultural heritage sitting unseen in storage. Traditional
restoration methods
, where conservators painstakingly fill damaged areas one at a time while mixing exact color matches for each region, can take weeks to decades for a single painting. It's skilled work that requires both artistic talent and deep technical knowledge, but there simply aren't enough conservators to tackle the backlog.
The mechanical engineering student conceived the idea during a 2021 cross-country drive to MIT, when gallery visits revealed how much art remains hidden due to damage and restoration backlogs. As someone who restores paintings as a hobby, he understood both the problem and the potential for a technological solution.
To demonstrate his method, Kachkine chose a challenging test case: a 15th-century oil painting requiring repairs in 5,612 separate regions. An AI model identified damage patterns and generated 57,314 different colors to match the original work. The entire restoration process reportedly took 3.5 hours—about 66 times faster than traditional hand-painting methods.
Alex Kachkine, who developed the AI-printed film technique.
Credit:
MIT
Notably, Kachkine avoided using generative AI models like
Stable Diffusion
or the "full-area application" of generative adversarial networks (GANs) for the digital restoration step. According to the Nature paper, these models cause "spatial distortion" that would prevent proper alignment between the restored image and the damaged original.
Instead, Kachkine utilized computer vision techniques found in prior art conservation research: "
cross-applied colouration
" for simple damages like thin cracks, and "
local partial convolution
" for reconstructing low-complexity patterns. For areas of high visual complexity, such as faces, Kachkine relied on traditional conservator methods, transposing features from other works by the same artist.
From pixels to polymers
Kachkine's process begins conventionally enough, with traditional cleaning to remove any previous restoration attempts. After scanning the cleaned painting, the aforementioned algorithms analyze the image and create a virtual restoration that "predicts" what the damaged areas should look like based on the surrounding paint and the artist's style. This part isn't particularly new—museums have been creating digital restorations for years. The innovative part is what happens next.
Custom software (
shared
by Kachkine online) maps every region needing repair and determines the exact colors required for each spot. His software then translates that information into a two-layer polymer mask printed on thin films—one layer provides color, while a white backing layer ensures the full color spectrum reproduces accurately on the painting's surface. The two layers must align precisely to reproduce colors accurately.
Overview of physically applied digital restoration.
High-fidelity inkjet printers produce the mask layers, which Kachkine aligns by hand and adheres to the painting using conservation-grade varnish spray. Importantly, the polymer materials dissolve in standard conservation solutions, allowing future removal of the mask without damaging the original work. Museums can also store digital files documenting every change made during restoration, creating a paper trail for future conservators.
Kachkine says that the technology doesn't replace human judgment—conservators must still guide ethical decisions about how much intervention is appropriate and whether digital predictions accurately capture the artist's original intent. data.title: Virtual cells
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了虚拟细胞（或全细胞模型，WCMs）的发展，这些数字化的细胞模型旨在通过计算机模拟生物细胞内的分子过程。文章追溯了这一领域的起源，从1952年Hodgkin和Huxley通过数学方程描述神经传导，到1990年代日本团队开发出首个E-Cell原型，尽管简陋，但首次在数字世界中模拟了细胞分裂。2012年，研究人员基于真实细菌Mycoplasma genitalium建立了首个完整的全细胞模型，通过删除基因模拟实验，发现了传统生物学注释中的错误，开启了数字细胞指导实际生物学研究的新时代。文章还提到该领域从模拟自然生命到设计合成生命的转变，尽管成本高昂，但前景广阔。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：合成生物学与细胞模拟的进展及其面临的挑战

不同观点：
• [hobofan] 认为合成最小细胞和虚拟细胞为生物化学实验提供了完全可控的环境，有助于从基础开始逐步理解细胞机制。他指出，目前生物化学研究往往受限于对细胞内已有机制的了解不足，导致大量实验需要试错。然而，当前很多努力集中于模拟包含未知机制的完整细胞，而不是利用这些能力生成假设以揭示未知机制。

• [nextos] 提到了过去二十年在细胞机制模型方面的大量工作，特别是通过常微分方程（ODEs）、偏微分方程（PDEs）和随机ODEs进行的研究。他指出高通量扰动分析推动了数据驱动的全细胞模型发展，但这些模型在做出可靠预测方面仍不够成熟。他认为未来可能是混合神经符号模型的天下。

• [maltee] 对文章和网站设计表示赞赏，特别提到参考论文和注释的质量。

• [moralestapia] 强调了自己在生物模拟领域的长期经验，并指出该领域的突破似乎近在咫尺但进展缓慢。他认为原因在于需要同时掌握多个学科的知识，包括生物学、化学、计算机科学、数学和物理学。他鼓励更多人加入这个领域，但同时也指出需要长时间的努力和学习。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是如何更好地推动细胞模拟的进展。hobofan认为应更多关注最小合成细胞的研究，以逐步揭示未知机制，而nextos则强调现有全细胞模型的局限性和未来混合模型的潜力。

• moralestapia的经验分享为理解该领域的复杂性和所需的多学科背景提供了有价值的视角，并指出了长期学习和研究的必要性。

44295725.article_content:
21 hours ago
in
Science
Virtual cells
Digital twins of biological cellsâoften referred to as
virtual cells
or
whole-cell models (WCMs)
âaim to recreate every relevant molecular process of a living cell
in silico
. This interdisciplinary endeavor marries systems biology, computational modeling, high-performance computing, and, increasingly, AI.
All models are wrong, but some are alive.
Somewhere in a data center right now, a virtual bacterium is dividing for the millionth time. Somewhere else, an AI-enhanced model is learning from a patient's tumor, preparing treatment recommendations that didn't exist when the sun rose. Biology has learned to debug itself, and we're just getting started.
This isn't science fictionâit's Tuesday morning in labs around the world. But the story of how we got here begins seventy years ago at the Marine Biological Association laboratory in Plymouthâa facility that would be bombed during the war, forcing the scientists to return years later to complete their revolutionary work.
From four to millions
Hodgkin-Huxley used 4 equations. Modern whole-cell models can contain tens of thousands of parameters and simulate millions of molecular interactions simultaneously.
In 1952, Alan Hodgkin and Andrew Huxley sat watching voltage traces flicker across an oscilloscope, capturing something no one had seen before: the precise mathematical choreography of a nerve firing. Their equations didn't just describe what happenedâthey predicted it, millisecond by millisecond. For the first time, life was speaking in the language of code.
A Quantitative Description of Membrane Current and its Application to Conduction and Excitation in Nerve
1952
~ A. L. Hodgkin & A. F. Huxley
This moment planted the seed for something extraordinary: the idea that we could build living systems entirely from code. But transforming that vision into reality would require decades of patient work, false starts, and technological leaps that no one could have predicted.
For forty years, the dream lay mostly dormant. Computers were too slow, biological data too sparse, and the sheer audacity of the goalâsimulating every molecule in a living cellâseemed to belong more in science fiction than serious research. Most biologists focused on understanding individual genes or proteins, not entire cellular systems.
Then in the late 1990s, a team of Japanese researchers decided to attempt the impossible. Working with the simplest hypothetical bacterium they could imagine, just 127 genes, they built the first prototype of what they called E-Cell. It was crude, crashed constantly, and bore only passing resemblance to any real organism. But when that virtual bacterium completed its first digital division cycle, something fundamental had shifted. A whole living system had been captured in code, however imperfectly.
Even so, the gap between simulation and reality remained vast. E-Cell was more proof of concept than practical tool. A sketch of what might be possible rather than a working model of life itself.
Assembling the data required reading and extracting parameters from 900+ scientific publications, creating the most comprehensive biological dataset ever compiled for a single organism.
The real turning point came more than a decade later, in 2012. This time, researchers weren't working with hypothetical organisms but with Mycoplasma genitalium, the simplest known free-living bacterium. They spent years extracting every measurable parameter from nearly a thousand research papersâreaction rates, protein concentrations, metabolic fluxesâbuilding what amounted to a molecular parts list for life itself.
A Whole-Cell Computational Model Predicts Phenotype from Genotype
2012
~ J. R. Karr et al.
When they finally assembled these fragments into 28 interconnected modules and hit run, the wait began. Ten hours of computation later, for the first time in history, an organismâhowever simpleâhad lived an entire life cycle inside a computer.
But here's what made it revolutionary: they immediately began breaking their virtual cell, deleting genes one by one to see what would happen. When certain deletions killed the simulation but left real bacteria unharmed, something profound was occurring. The model was revealing errors in decades of biological annotations. The digital cell had become teacher to its carbon counterpart.
This reversed relationshipâsilicon instructing carbonâmarked the beginning of a new chapter in biology.
The field exploded from there, but in directions no one had anticipated. Rather than simply making existing models more complex, researchers began asking a different question:
what if we could design life from scratch, then simulate our own creations?
It is estimated that the synthetic genome used for this project cost an estimated $40 million and 200 person-years of workâmaking. It one of the most expensive single cells ever built. Yet even this stripped-down organism holds secrets we're still unraveling

data.title: DNA floating in the air tracks wildlife, viruses, even drugs
data.author: karlperera
data.article_summary: 科学家通过使用高功率空气过滤器和环境DNA（eDNA）分析，在爱尔兰都柏林的空气中发现了野生动物、毒品和病原体的遗传物质。这项技术无需与生物直接接触，可以用来监控生态系统、追踪疾病，甚至定位濒危物种。研究团队从空气中收集到了大麻、迷幻蘑菇以及数百种人类病原体的DNA，展示了其广泛应用潜力。该方法高效快速，单个研究人员一天内即可处理多种物种的DNA，有助于疾病监测和过敏原追踪。然而，由于可能涉及敏感的人类遗传信息，研究人员呼吁建立伦理规范。这项技术正将科幻变为现实。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于DNA测序技术的发展及其隐私、伦理和安全问题的讨论。

不同观点：
• [arjie] 认为将自己的DNA序列公开存储存在风险，表达了对公开DNA可能带来的后果的担忧，甚至表示自己可能成为反面教材。
• [robwwilliams] 从技术角度出发，指出在处理人类或低模板DNA时需要极度谨慎，以防止空气中的DNA污染，提到了PCR扩增中的技术细节。
• [altacc] 感叹技术进步的速度，从人类基因组测序需要13年到现在可以快速从空气中获取DNA，表达了对技术进步的惊讶。
• [karlperera] 提出了技术普及和低成本化后的隐私问题，指出能够从公共或私人空间中获取人类漂浮DNA可能带来的伦理困境，提出了“我们能否/应否这样做”的问题。

补充讨论：
• [strangattractor] 以幽默方式提到了Farnsworth Smell-O-Scope，暗示这种技术类似于科幻作品中的发明。
• [kylehotchkiss] 将此问题视为信噪比的问题，可能是在讨论技术实现中的挑战。
• [aspenmayer] 提到过去利用小型吸尘器秘密收集DNA的案例，引用了维基百科上关于追捕本拉登的例子，强调了这种技术在情报工作中的应用历史。
• [m3kw9] 以幽默方式提出了“狗能闻到DNA”的观点，可能是在调侃DNA检测技术与嗅觉的关系。
• [tekla] 提到了“Hoovers”这一旧称，只是建议继续使用旧名称，未深入讨论技术问题。

争议焦点：
• 公开DNA数据的隐私和安全风险，以及技术快速发展带来的伦理问题。
• 技术普及后的隐私保护与技术应用之间的平衡问题。

44287926.article_content:
Science News
from research organizations
DNA floating in the air tracks wildlife, viruses -- even drugs
Date:
June 3, 2025
Source:
University of Florida
Summary:
In the heart of Dublin, scientists have discovered that the air holds more than melodies and Guinness-infused cheer it carries invisible traces of life, from wildlife to drugs and even human diseases. Using high-powered air filters and environmental DNA (eDNA) analysis, researchers vacuumed up the city s air and uncovered genetic material from cannabis, magic mushrooms, and pathogens. This emerging technology, which doesn t require direct contact with organisms, could revolutionize how we monitor ecosystems, track diseases, and even locate endangered species all from the sky above. It's science fiction turned science fact, and it s changing what we thought was possible from a simple breath of air.
Share:
Facebook
Twitter
Pinterest
LinkedIN
Email
FULL STORY
DNA floating in the air over Dublin revealed everything from wildlife to illegal drugs. Scientists used air filters to collect eDNA, showing that we can track species and pathogens invisibly, without ever seeing them. Credit: Shutterstock
Dublin is known as a city where you can enjoy a few pints of Guiness, get a warm welcome from the locals and hear lively traditional music drifting out of pubs and into the city air.
But it's not just music floating on the breeze. The air of Dublin also contains cannabis, poppy, even magic mushrooms -- at least their DNA.
That's according to a new study that reveals the power of DNA, vacuumed up from the air, which can track everything from elusive bobcats to illicit drugs.
"The level of information that's available in environmental DNA is such that we're only starting to consider what the potential applications can be, from humans, to wildlife to other species that have implications for human health," said David Duffy, Ph.D., a professor of wildlife disease genomics at the University of Florida and lead author of a new study showing the widespread utility of DNA vacuumed from the air.
Housed at UF's Whitney Laboratory for Marine Bioscience, Duffy's lab developed new methods for deciphering environmental DNA, also known as eDNA, to study sea turtle genetics. They've expanded the tools to study every species -- including humans -- from DNA captured in environmental samples like water, soil and sand.
But these errant strands of DNA do not just settle into muddy soil or flow along rivers. The air itself is infused with genetic material. A simple air filter running for hours, days or weeks can pick up signs of nearly every species that grows or wanders nearby.
"When we started, it seemed like it would be hard to get intact large fragments of DNA from the air. But that's not the case. We're actually finding a lot of informative DNA," Duffy said. "That means you can study species without directly having to disturb them, without ever having to see them. It opens up huge possibilities to study all the species in an area simultaneously, from microbes and viruses all the way up to vertebrates like bobcats and humans, and everything in between."
As a proof of concept, the researchers showed that they could pick up signs of hundreds of different human pathogens from the Dublin air, including viruses and bacteria. Such surveillance could help scientists track emerging diseases. The same method can track common allergens, like peanut or pollen, more precisely than is currently possible, the scientists discovered.
In another test of the power of eDNA, Duffy's lab was also able to identify the origin of bobcats and spiders whose DNA was hoovered up from air in a Florida forest. With little more than an air filter, scientists could track endangered species and identify where they came from, all without having to lay eyes on skittish animals or root around forest floors for scat samples. When trying to save and conserve wildlife, knowing where an animal originates from can be as important as knowing where it currently is.
This powerful analysis was paired with impressive speed and efficiency. The team demonstrated that a single researcher could process DNA for every species in as little as a day using compact, affordable equipment, and software hosted in the cloud. That quick turnaround is orders of magnitude faster than would have been possible just a few years ago and opens up advanced environmental studies to more scientists around the world. The same tools can potentially identify sensitive human genetic data, which is why Duffy and his collaborators have called for ethical guardrails for the rapidly developing field of eDNA.
"It seems like science fiction, but it's becoming science fact," Duffy said. "The technology is finally matching the scale of environmental problems."

主要讨论点：新冠病毒（COVID-19）及其长期后遗症（Long Covid）的影响，特别是对青少年的影响、疫苗与后遗症的区分以及科学研究的必要性。

不同观点：

data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了为何某些生态系统容易被外来物种入侵，而其他则能抵抗入侵。基于Charles Elton 1958年的理论，多样性高的生态系统应更能抵御入侵，因为资源已被充分使用。然而，后续研究发现，有些多样性高的生态系统仍会被入侵。麻省理工学院的物理学家Jeff Gore通过在实验室中用微生物模拟生态网络，发现入侵在多样性高的微生物生态系统中更可能发生，尤其当物种数量随时间波动时。这一动态视角揭示了时间对生态系统入侵的影响，提供了更细致的研究方法。文章强调了理解生态系统内在动态机制对预测入侵成功的重要性。

The Ecosystem Dynamics That Can Make or Break an Invasion

By simulating ecological networks with microbes, researchers revealed properties that may make natural communities susceptible to invasion.
