The short explanation: The Wikimedia wikis get blocked or users might be tracked as they edit. This is one of ways in which the Wikimedia Foundation SRE/Traffic team tries to combat those problems.
Wikimedia DNS
(formerly called
Wikidough
), is a caching, recursive, public
DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH)
and
DNS-over-TLS (DoT)
resolver service that is run and managed by the Site Reliability Engineering (Traffic) team at the Foundation. Wikimedia DNS helps prevent some surveillance and censorship of our wikis and other websites by securing DNS lookups.
This document outlines what the service is about, why the SRE/Traffic team is working on it, and what benefits it provides for the Wikimedia community. We welcome any discussions about this project on the
talk page
.
Introduction to DNS
[
edit
]
What is DNS?
[
edit
]
The
Domain Name System
(DNS) is the phonebook of the internet. It provides a lookup of domain names (such as wikipedia.org) to their IP addresses (
208.80.154.224
). Whenever you visit a resource on the internet like a website, a DNS resolver — typically run by your
Internet Service Provider
(ISP) — resolves the domain to an IP address and is the first step in the creation of a connection to a website. Without the IP address you won't be able to find the right website. This process happens in the background and because of the way the internet works, most people automatically connect to their ISP's DNS resolver to perform these DNS queries.
DNS is a critical part of the internet and DNS lookups happen regardless of which resource you want to access or where you access it from (mobile or phone).
DNS-based surveillance and censorship
[
edit
]
Even though DNS has been around for decades, a DNS query (
what is the IP address of wikipedia.org?
) and the response (
the IP address is 208.80.154.224
) are not encrypted. This is a significant privacy and security risk. An on-path observer — such as your coffee shop, ISP, or your government — can observe your DNS queries/responses and build a list of the resources you access on the internet, and perhaps worse, censor you by preventing access to content they deem unacceptable.
Since we are primarily concerned with censorship in the context of the movement, Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects have been censored through DNS and this has been observed in
various countries
where we are active. DNS censorship is easy to implement, scales effectively, and also since DNS is the first step in the connection to a remote resource, most ISPs and governments use DNS censorship to prevent people from accessing content on the internet.
As an example, censoring queries for
*.wikipedia.org
to prevent people from accessing any language edition of Wikipedia is trivial to implement in most DNS resolver software and is a one-line change.
DNS encryption
[
edit
]
To solve the problem of surveillance and censorship of DNS, various DNS encryption protocols have been proposed over the years. Due to various reasons including a lack of a standard, adaptability, implementation, none of the proposed protocols have seen mass adoption until DNS-over-HTTPS was
proposed and standardized
in 2018. The Mozilla Firefox browser helped push adoption of DoH by enabling it by
default for US users in 2020
and has since rolled this out to other countries as well.
DoH and DoT
[
edit
]
DNS-over-HTTPS
, also called DoH, encrypts DNS by sending queries and getting responses over HTTPS, thus preventing censorship and surveillance: because an on-path observer can no longer see the queries or the responses, they cannot censor it or build a profile of the data. DoH works by sending DNS queries over a secure HTTPS channel.
DNS-over-TLS
, also called DoT, is a related DNS encryption protocol offering encryption over just TLS. It hasn't seen the same rate of adoption DNS-over-HTTPS has seen for various reasons that we will discuss later. Nevertheless, we consider both of these protocols related for the purpose of this discussion and the Wikimedia DNS service, even though there are differences between them at the protocol level.
To use this new DNS encryption technology, you need a DoH- or DoT-enabled client and a resolver.
Wikimedia DNS
[
edit
]
Wikimedia DNS is a public DNS-over-HTTPS and DNS-over-TLS resolver service. For users who wish to secure their DNS lookups to prevent surveillance or to circumvent DNS-based censorship, Wikimedia DNS helps protect your DNS queries/responses by providing encryption of the same. data.article_summary:
本文由Steve Yegge于2025年6月18日撰写，概述了自3月份以来编程领域的主要变化，特别是自主编码代理工具的兴起。文章提到，自"Revenge of the Junior Developer"（RotJD）发布以来的三个月中，模型技术显著进步，如Claude 3.7和OpenAI的Codex等工具正解决以往无法解决的问题。Sourcegraph推出的Amp则是面向团队的编码代理工具，受到用户好评。

文章还介绍了作者与Gene Kim合著的关于“氛围编码”（vibe coding）的书籍，并提到与Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei的会面。文章预测了开发工作、知识工作及社会的变化，强调了学习使用编码代理工具或掌握一门手艺的重要性。

最后，文章详细描述了“代理编码”（agentic coding）的概念，指出这种新方式正迅速取代传统IDE，开发者通过AI生成代码，审查差异并测试输出，形成新的工作流程。

Back to blog
The Brute Squad
Steve Yegge
June 18, 2025
Welcome back! Come one, come all, friends, foes, fart connoisseurs, all are welcome here at Camel Central. It has been an action-packed three months since
Revenge of the Junior Developer
(RotJD), which is essential reading for this post, so shoo, off you go. You might also want to watch The Princess Bride, up to you. As you wish!
What has changed since March? Much and little, more or less. For starters, models got better. Claude 3.7, every programmer's favorite, is now nearly four months old, one foot already in the grave, sounding like a talking parrot compared to the newer models. Recent releases from Anthropic, OpenAI and Google are chewing through problems that were unsolvable by their predecessors. At least on my box. We're still on those curves, right on schedule.
We've also got a crop of exciting autonomous-agent tools, the so-called camels that are replacing all that walking you're doing with Cursor right now. For instance, in response to the game-changing Claude Code, OpenAI launched their own coding agent, which they named
Codex
, in a clever nod to how nobody can understand any of their model names or when they came out or how they relate to each other or which one is better for any given task. Codex is ideal for anyone who understands that stuff, e.g. presumably certain OpenAI employees, possibly some of the models themselves.
Rounding out the trio, Sourcegraph launched Amp, which is a team-oriented enterprise coding agent, with leaderboards, public workstreams, and friendly competition. People are finding Amp refreshing and our users are effusive about it; even Swyx gave it a nod recently (yo Swyx!)
So now you have choices. Claude Code, Codex, and Amp: three serious commercial autonomous coding agent contenders. And there are also some great OSS agents improving fast, like Cline and RooCode, for which I have high hopes.
What else is new since March? I am relieved to report that I have at long last finished co-authoring a book on vibe coding, along with my buddy, famed writer/researcher Gene Kim. It was a months-long slog for us to make it an hours-long read. It's our instruction manual for vibe coding, both with chat and with autonomous agents. Vibe coding professionally is a complex craft, and a topic for another day. But I'll drop a link at the end, and I'll be posting more about it soon.
One other small bit of news, prompted in part by RotJD, is that in April I got to meet Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, for a private half hour 1:1 chat at their HQ. Unfortunately on the way over, my brain received a remote firmware downgrade, leaving me with the intelligence and personality of a sea cucumber for approximately thirty-five minutes. But it was a delightful discussion, uh, for me, and I will share some of the highlights toward the end of the post.
And with that, on with the show! Our production today features more of everything you loved from RotJD. In this post you'll be treated to crazy news and crazier stories that touch on three themes: 1) Dev work is changing, 2) Knowledge work is changing, and 3) Society is changing. We'll have more predictions, more facts, and more flatulence; I leave it to you to decide what's what.
If you don't like long form reading, then, TL;DR:Â  Either learn to use coding agents, or start learning a trade. I hear electricians drive the nicest cars on the construction sites. And
plumbers are the new millionaire class
. You've got options.
I prefer long form stories though, don't you? You laugh, you cry, you remember it forever. If you're down, let's go!
â
Part 1: The Death of the IDE
Today's first exciting topic: all your favorite software development tools are getting killed off faster than a new Netflix series. What, you say? Who shot who in the what now?
Well, not exactly killed off per se. Dying off, more like. They're being replaced by agentic coding: a brand new way to develop software since February, exponentially gaining popularity all around you, though you may be blissfully oblivious. Agentic coding is short for "vibe coding with autonomous coding agents." The typical agentic coding workflow doesn't involve using traditional IDEs like, say, Cursor, or Windsurf. In the limit, you don't use them at all.
Instead, agentic coding is console based, 1970s-style, in a text terminal window with little to no UI. The developer workflow is simple: You ask the AI for code changes, then you review the diffs and test the output, in a loop, lather, rinse, repeat. It's a bit like you're directing a movie, but micromanaging the crew's work more obsessively than Stanley Kubrick. It can be both as fun and as stressful as directing a movie, but once you start, you never go back to the old way.
A buddy at Anthropic told me that engineers there rarely use their IDEs anymore. To agentic vibe coders, opening an IDE is like opening the Chrome developer tools, or maybe popping the hood on your Uber: an undesirable scenario, a m

data.title: Researchers using the same data and hypothesis arrive at different conclusions (2022)
data.author: like_any_other
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：科学研究的可信性及结论的客观性

不同观点：
• [cdot2] 认为社会学等学科的数据和结论之间缺乏相关性，因此不能被视为“科学”，并将这些学科与占星学和颅相学相提并论，暗示其缺乏科学性。

• [delichon] 提出数据和假设应与结论分开发布，以确保研究者的结论不会被赋予特权。这样可以让同行评审更加中立，专注于数据本身，而结论则可以根据其自身的优点被单独评估。如果实验者比其他人更了解自己的数据，那么说明他们没有提供足够的数据。

• [fhsm] 指出该文章在2022年已经流行过，表示内容有趣但并不新颖，暗示讨论的主题缺乏时效性和新意。

• [alphazard] 建议科学家应通过押注第三方进行的实验结果来获得收入，这样可以为已有理论提供小而稳定的现金流，而突破性发现则会带来巨大的单次收益。同时，这种机制也能惩罚那些阻碍突破性发现的固有观念。为了实现这一点，实验必须由与研究者无关的第三方进行。

补充讨论：
• [delichon] 的观点强调了科学研究过程中数据透明性和同行评审独立性的重要性，认为这样可以避免研究者的结论对评审过程产生不当影响。

• [alphazard] 的建议引入了一种经济激励机制，以促进科学研究的客观性和创新性，同时通过第三方实验来确保结果的公正性。

争议焦点：
• 争议的焦点在于社会学等学科是否具备足够的科学性，以及如何确保科学研究结论的客观性和可信性。具体讨论了数据与结论的分离发布、同行评审的独立性以及科学激励机制的创新。

data.title: HIV vaccine candidate could offer strong protection with just one dose
data.author: jnord
data.article_summary: MIT和斯克里普斯研究所的研究人员通过在HIV疫苗中添加两种强效佐剂，实现了一次接种即可产生强大的免疫反应。这两种佐剂帮助疫苗在淋巴结中积累，并持续长达一个月，刺激B细胞产生更多样化和高亲和力的抗体。相比单一佐剂或无佐剂疫苗，这种双佐剂策略显著增强了小鼠对HIV抗原的免疫反应。这种方法不仅适用于HIV疫苗，还可能用于开发针对SARS-CoV-2、流感等疾病的一次性疫苗。研究成果发表在《Science Translational Medicine》上，由J. Christopher Love和Darrell Irvine领导。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：盖茨基金会是否会资助特别是在撒哈拉以南非洲地区部署一次性治疗方案，以解决结核病（TB）持续存在的问题。

不同观点：
• 观点一：盖茨基金会可能会资助在撒哈拉以南非洲地区部署一次性治疗方案，因为这种方案能够克服多次注射的阻力，并且不需要持续的资金来维持药物供应链。这种方案有助于解决由于缺乏资金而无法持续提供药物的问题，从而有效对抗结核病的持续蔓延。

• 观点二：有人可能认为，即使有一次性治疗方案，部署和推广依然面临诸多挑战，包括基础设施不足、医疗系统薄弱以及其他经济和政治因素，这些都可能影响盖茨基金会是否会选择资助此类项目。

Researchers at MIT and the Scripps Research Institute have shown that they can generate a strong immune response to HIV with just one vaccine dose, by adding two powerful adjuvants — materials that help stimulate the immune system.
In a study of mice, the researchers showed that this approach produced a much wider diversity of antibodies against an HIV antigen, compared to the vaccine given on its own or with just one of the adjuvants. The dual-adjuvant vaccine accumulated in the lymph nodes and remained there for up to a month, allowing the immune system to build up a much greater number of antibodies against the HIV protein.
This strategy could lead to the development of vaccines that only need to be given once, for infectious diseases including HIV or SARS-CoV-2, the researchers say.
“This approach is compatible with many protein-based vaccines, so it offers the opportunity to engineer new formulations for these types of vaccines across a wide range of different diseases, such as influenza, SARS-CoV-2, or other pandemic outbreaks,” says J. Christopher Love, the Raymond A. and Helen E. St. Laurent Professor of Chemical Engineering at MIT, and a member of the Koch Institute for Integrative Cancer Research and the Ragon Institute of MGH, MIT, and Harvard.
Love and Darrell Irvine, a professor of immunology and microbiology at the Scripps Research Institute, are the senior authors of the study, which appears today in
Science Translational Medicine
. Kristen Rodrigues PhD ’23 and Yiming Zhang PhD ’25 are the lead authors of the
paper
.
More powerful vaccines
Most vaccines are delivered along with adjuvants, which help to stimulate a stronger immune response to the antigen. One adjuvant commonly used with protein-based vaccines, including those for hepatitis A and B, is aluminum hydroxide, also known as alum. This adjuvant works by activating the innate immune response, helping the body to form a stronger memory of the vaccine antigen.
Several years ago, Irvine developed another adjuvant based on saponin, an FDA-approved adjuvant derived from the bark of the Chilean soapbark tree. His work showed that
nanoparticles
containing both saponin and a molecule called MPLA, which promotes inflammation, worked better than saponin on its own. That nanoparticle, known as SMNP, is now being used as an adjuvant for an HIV vaccine that is currently in
clinical trials
.
Irvine and Love then tried combining alum and SMNP and showed that vaccines containing both of those adjuvants could generate even more powerful immune responses against either HIV or SARS-CoV-2.
In the new paper, the researchers wanted to explore why these two adjuvants work so well together to boost the immune response, specifically the B cell response. B cells produce antibodies that can circulate in the bloodstream and recognize a pathogen if the body is exposed to it again.
For this study, the researchers used an HIV protein called MD39 as their vaccine antigen, and anchored dozens of these proteins to each alum particle, along with SMNP.
After vaccinating mice with these particles, the researchers found that the vaccine accumulated in the lymph nodes — structures where B cells encounter antigens and undergo rapid mutations that generate antibodies with high affinity for a particular antigen. This process takes place within clusters of cells known as germinal centers.

data.title: YouTube's new anti-adblock measures
data.author: smitop
data.article_summary: YouTube正在测试新的反广告拦截措施，其中一种措施是“假缓冲”，即在视频开始时故意延迟加载。测试中的“假缓冲”时间约为广告时长的80%，即使使用广告拦截器，用户仍能节省时间。该措施通过InnerTube API和GVS（Google Video Services）系统实现，在视频请求中加入回退指令，导致延迟。作者发现了一种方法，通过修改uBlock Origin和Brave浏览器的过滤规则，在JSON请求中加入"isInlinePlaybackNoAd":true，从而避免广告和假缓冲。网络上有关CPU损坏的传言是不实的，假缓冲不会对计算机造成损害。

44329712.article_content:
Over the past few months, YouTube has been trying another round of anti-adblock measures. Currently the anti-adblock stuff is being A/B tested, and one of my accounts is in the experimental group. I wrote a filter that partially avoids one of the anti-adblock measures, fake buffering, on uBlock Origin (and Brave browser, since it uses the same filter rules). (It’s already in the default filter lists, you don’t need to manually add the filter.)
One thing that people have ran into is “fake buffering”, where videos will take a while to load due to a lot of buffering, but only at the very start of the video (there’s no mid-video fake buffering). As I’ll explain, the fake buffering is 80% of the length of the ads you would’ve seen, so even with fake buffering you’re still saving time using an adblocker.
Context
InnerTube is YouTubeâs first party internal API that the web client and mobile apps use to interact with videos and get details about them. InnerTube endpoints look like
https://www.youtube.com/youtubei/
. One of those endpoints is
/youtubei/v1/player
, which the web client calls when you click on a video to get data about the URL and GVS stream URLs.
GVS (Google Video Services) is a service that serves video streams for YouTube, Google Drive, and Google Photos. To stream a video from GVS, you need to get a GVS
/videoplayback
URL from InnerTube (or the Drive/Photos internal API). GVS URLs are signed and have an expiry time (usually 6 hours), so you canât construct them on your own, you need to get one from InnerTube. One weird thing about GVS is that it isnât only hosted from Googleâs data center: ISPs can put
Google Global Cache
servers in their infrastructure so that they can serve YouTube videos without needing to send traffic outside the ISPâs network (only public/unlisted YouTube videos are served by GGC; private YT videos and Drive/Photos videos are always served from Google data centers). GVS URLs look like
https://rr1---sn-gvbxgn-tt1e6.googlevideo.com/videoplayback?expire=1750321185&...
(but with a lot more query parameters).
Originally the web client streamed video by just using some query parameters to the GVS URL to specify what range of video it wanted, and GVS responded with the video contents for that range. But for complicated reasons, YouTube decided to improve on this with SABR (Server ABR (Adaptive Bit Rate)), which is YouTubeâs proprietary binary protocol for streaming video data, which is better at avoiding buffering than todayâs open formats (e.g. MPEG-DASH). One thing that SABR supports is the server sending a backoff to the client, instructing the client to wait some amount of time before trying again instead of sending video/audio data.
The source of fake buffering
Whatâs happening is that InnerTube is providing GVS streams that will give a backoff of 80% of the ad duration for ads for the first
/videoplayback
request (for the content video, not the ads), so for example if the ad is 15 seconds youâll get 12 seconds of backoff when blocking ads. If you have an unskippable 6 second ad AND a 15 second unskippable ad together the backoff will be 16.8 seconds. To be clear this isnât server-side ad insertion; the ad and content streams are still separate (YouTube
is
doing a server-side ad insertion experiment, but thatâs separate from fake buffering). The âExperiencing interruptionsâ dialogs are likely triggered by long backoffs from GVS.
This backoff
always
happen if you’re in the A/B test, regardless of if YouTube thinks you’re using an adblocker. You just don’t notice it if you’re not blocking ads, because the web client starts loading the content video while the ad plays, so the only difference for non-ad-blocking users is that the content video doesn’t start buffering until the ad is 80% over.
Iâve seen claims online that YouTube is âDAMAGING Computers By SPIKING CPU Usage If You Use Ad Blockâ. This is completely false; YouTube doesnât use CPU usage waiting for the backoff to expire (and even if they used a spinloop to implement the wait, maxing a single core for <30 seconds wonât damage any CPU).
Become unadvertisable
How can you avoid getting backoffed until the unskippable ad is over? Donât get served an ad in the first place. If you set the
playbackContext.
contentPlaybackContext.
isInlinePlaybackNoAd
property in player requests to true, InnerTube wonât serve you any ads and thus wonât include any backoff in the GVS streams.
We can write a filter rule that makes it so whenever the web client stringifies JSON bound for a server request, we add
"isInlinePlaybackNoAd":true
to the stringified JSON.

data.article_summary: Yggdrasil是一种实验性紧凑路由方案，旨在为互联网提供去中心化、面向未来的路由协议，并支持大规模mesh网络。其特点包括可扩展、自愈、加密、以及纯 peer-to-peer 架构，且跨平台支持。当前版本为轻量级用户空间软件路由器，易于配置，支持端到端加密IPv6路由，可通过TCP/TLS建立节点连接。尽管仍处于alpha阶段，但已具备日常使用的稳定性，并有一小部分用户进行各种测试。感兴趣的用户可以通过安装和配置加入网络，探索内部服务，参与开发和反馈问题。

Yggdrasil is a new experimental compact routing scheme. It is designed to be a future-proof and decentralised alternative to the structured routing protocols commonly used today on the Internet, as well as an enabling technology for future large-scale mesh networks. Yggdrasil is:
Scalable
Supports large, complex or even Internet-scale topologies
Self-healing
Network responds quickly to connection failures or mobility events
Encrypted
Traffic sent across the network is always fully end-to-end encrypted
Peer-to-peer
Works entirely ad-hoc by design with no built-in points of centralisation
Cross-platform
Supported on Linux, macOS, Windows, iOS, Android and more
The
current implementation
of Yggdrasil is a lightweight userspace software router which is easy to configure and supported on a wide range of platforms. It provides end-to-end encrypted IPv6 routing between all network participants. Peerings between nodes can be configured using TCP/TLS connections over local area networks, point-to-point links or the Internet. Even though the Yggdrasil Network provides IPv6 routing between nodes, peering connections can be set up over either IPv4 or IPv6 networks.
This is still an alpha-stage project and there may be some breaking changes in the future. Despite that, Yggdrasil is generally stable enough for day-to-day use and a small number of users have been using and stress-testing Yggdrasil quite heavily for a variety of use cases. If you are interested in or would like to get involved in the Yggdrasil project, start below:
Install
and
configure
Yggdrasil on your own computer or router to join the network.
Explore the
internal services
available on the network operated by our users.
Visit our
developers
page and our
GitHub
. Report bugs and problems to us as
GitHub Issues
.

• **kemotep的观点**：质疑为何德州选择比特币作为战略储备，而不是像石油储备或多元化投资的主权财富基金那样更传统的资产。他将比特币储备比作德州决定购买大量单一股票（如Nvidia或Tesla），暗示这种做法缺乏多样化和风险管理。

  - bediger4000指出，他不明白比特币储备在实际应急中的作用，表明对这种新型资产的实用性缺乏信心。
  - kemotep通过类比战略石油储备和主权财富基金，强调传统储备资产的多样化和稳定性，暗示比特币缺乏这些优点。

data.author: rmast
data.article_summary: MSI Viewer and Extractor 是一款在线工具，允许用户在浏览器中查看和提取MSI文件的内容，且所有操作均在本地设备上完成，无需将文件上传至服务器。该工具使用Pyodide运行pymsi，提供查看MSI文件的详细信息，包括文件列表、表格数据、摘要信息和流内容等功能。用户可以选择MSI文件进行查看和提取所有文件（打包为ZIP格式）。该工具由Lawrence Livermore National Security提供，文档使用Sphinx和Alabaster构建。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：MSI文件处理工具的改进建议及使用体验

不同观点：
• simonw: 认为工具很酷，并建议添加一个示例MSI文件和"加载示例文件"按钮，以便没有MSI文件的用户也能试用。
• pragma_x: 认为该工具解决了只需打印机驱动文件而不需要其他内容的需求，对工作表示赞赏。
• danielodievich: 回忆MSI初期工具不完善的经历，感叹如今能在浏览器中打开MSI文件的进步，并对工作表示赞赏。
• Lanrei: 提到通常使用7zip来打开.exe和.msi文件，暗示这是一种常见的替代方法。
• rmast: 分享在iPhone的Safari浏览器上尝试检查MSI文件的体验，指出检查功能可用，但对提取文件的功能存有疑问。

补充讨论：
• 工具的潜在改进：simonw的建议旨在提高工具的易用性和用户体验。
• 历史背景：danielodievich提供了MSI工具发展的历史视角，强调了当前工具的进步。
• 替代方法：Lanrei指出了使用7zip作为处理MSI文件的常见替代方法。
• 移动端体验：rmast提供了在移动设备上使用该工具的反馈，提出了对提取文件功能的疑问。
• 争议焦点：目前没有明显的争议，但rmast对移动端提取文件功能的疑问可能需要进一步验证和澄清。

data.title: I went for 1,200 jobs but got only two interviews
data.author: spzb
data.article_summary: 德安娜·伍德豪斯-霍金斯（Deanna Woodhouse-Hawkins），一名25岁的伯明翰毕业生，拥有开放大学（Open University）的计算机与信息技术学位，但在18个月内申请超过1,200个职位后仅获得两次面试机会。她表示，求职过程令她感到沮丧，因从未收到雇主的反馈。在申请过程中，她因焦虑和抑郁问题而苦苦挣扎，最终通过一个名为Generation UK的项目获得了当前的初级Python开发员职位。该项目帮助她提升了简历撰写、面试技巧及技术能力。项目负责人凯尔西·弗林（Kelsey Flynn）指出，年轻人的失业率正在上升，许多人缺乏获取培训和支持的机会。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：就业市场的变化和求职难度

不同观点：
• **stevage**：回顾2004年时，毕业生找工作相对容易。他提到自己当时并不特别想得到一份工作，但仍然获得了面试机会并最终被录用。他通过个人经历说明过去找工作相对轻松，而现在可能变得更加困难。

• **Noumenon72**：认为即便在2000年时求职压力已经很大，而现在可能更大。他提到自己通过学习编程后很少需要求职，但每次求职都会拖延很久。他对招聘人员帮助求职者通过繁琐的求职流程表示感激，并希望每个人都能有类似的帮助。

• **Dfiesl**：质疑有人能在18个月内投递1200份求职申请的质量。他认为这种高频率的投递无法让求职者找到真正感兴趣的工作，也无法让他们在每次拒绝后反思和改进自己的求职策略，更无法写出有效的求职信。

• **susiecambria**：分享了1990年代在非营利组织工作的经历，强调了对求职者进行跟进反馈的重要性。她创建了一种明信片来回复未被录用的求职者，并表示这种反馈机制在她的组织中并不普遍，令她感到不满。

• **gngoo**：指出计算机科学（CS）教育与快速变化的就业市场之间的脱节。他认为即使是资金充足的大学也难以跟上行业变化，社区学院更不用说。他质疑目前谁还会雇佣没有经验的初级开发者，并表达了对LLM（大型语言模型）可能取代部分编程工作的担忧。

• **Spivak**：认为现在的求职申请大多石沉大海，除非通过某种人际网络获得内部推荐。他强调了人际关系在求职中的重要性，认为不通过网上申请表投递简历是获得面试机会的唯一途径。

• **culopatin**：对原帖中的抱怨持怀疑态度，认为缺乏足够的信息来判断求职失败的原因。他质疑求职者的学历背景、简历质量和项目经验，认为单凭“感到悲伤和压力”无法说明问题。

补充讨论：
• 求职市场的变化：多个评论者提到过去求职相对容易，而现在竞争更加激烈，求职者需要更多策略和外部帮助。
• 反馈机制的缺失：susiecambria强调了求职反馈的重要性，而其他评论者则没有提到这一点，显示出反馈机制在求职过程中的稀缺性。
• 人际关系和内部推荐：Spivak和Noumenon72提到通过人际网络获得求职机会的重要性，这与单纯依赖网上申请表形成对比。
• 教育与市场需求脱节：gngoo对CS教育无法跟上行业变化表示担忧，并质疑初级职位的存在和求职者的竞争力。

争议焦点：当前求职难度是否被夸大，以及求职失败的原因是否仅归因于市场变化和教育脱节，还是与求职者自身条件（如学历、简历质量、项目经验）有关。

44341199.article_content:
Image source,
Generation UK
Image caption,
Deanna Woodhouse-Hawkins, 25, graduated with a Computing and IT Degree through the Open University
Shehnaz Khan
BBC News, West Midlands
Published
21 June 2025
A woman who struggled to find a job after graduating from university said she applied for more than 1,200 roles - but only secured two interviews.
Deanna Woodhouse-Hawkins, 25, from Birmingham, applied for the positions over a period of 18 months, after graduating with a degree in computing and IT through the Open University.
Ms Woodhouse-Hawkins found it impossible to find a job in her field and said she never received any feedback from potential employers on her applications.
"It was depressing," she told the BBC. "You'd think you'd get more [interviews] as you apply and you'd tailor these CVs and you just hear nothing back."
"Even when you do the assessments they ask you to do, you either don't hear anything back and if you do it's just usually, 'Oh, you haven't passed'," she added.
Image source,
Generation UK
Image caption,
Kelsey Flynn, from Generation UK, said the firm trained people for entry level jobs with a skills shortage
Ms Woodhouse-Hawkins, who lives in Quinton, eventually found a role as a Junior Python (widespread computing language) Developer at Global Telecoms Networks, where she has just completed her three-month probation.
After struggling with her mental health throughout the job application process alongside claiming Universal Credit, she received help from a foundation that offers support to unemployed people get set up with tech careers in the West Midlands.
She said the programme, run by Generation UK, "instilled hope" that she would finally get a job in a field she had trained for.
A skills boot-camp, between October 2024 and January, taught her how to craft a CV that stands out, as well as interview techniques and additional technical skills that were missing from her Open University curriculum.
'Getting ghosted'
Ms Woodhouse-Hawkins suffers from anxiety and depression and said the main reason her mental health plummeted was because she got no feedback from potential employers.
Out of more than 1,000 applications, she only secured a job interview for her current role and one previous application.
"It was just literally, applying for jobs, not hearing back, getting ghosted," she said of the process.
"Tailoring your CV to try and get a response. Not getting a response and if you do get a response it's very generic of, 'Oh we've moved onto a different candidate', or someone else fits the job better.
"It's just all the same usual, just being ghosted."
Kelsey Flynn, head of impact at Generation UK, said Ms Woodhouse-Hawkins' experience of rejection after rejection was "far too common".
"We see it all the time," she said.  "Unemployment amongst young people is on the rise and it's really scary.
"Most of the people that we come across desperately want careers and are really trying to find them. But they just need access to the training and support."

• **gngoo**：指出计算机科学（CS）教育与快速变化的就业市场之间的脱节。他认为即使是资金充足的大学也难以跟上行业变化，社区学院更不用说。他质疑目前谁还会雇佣没有经验的初级开发者，并表达了对LLM（大型语言模型）可能取代部分编程工作的担忧。

• **Spivak**：认为现在的求职申请大多石沉大海，除非通过某种人际网络获得内部推荐。他强调了人际关系在求职中的重要性，认为不通过网上申请表投递简历是获得面试机会的唯一途径。

• **culopatin**：对原帖中的抱怨持怀疑态度，认为缺乏足够的信息来判断求职失败的原因。他质疑求职者的学历背景、简历质量和项目经验，认为单凭“感到悲伤和压力”无法说明问题。

补充讨论：
• 求职市场的变化：多个评论者提到过去求职相对容易，而现在竞争更加激烈，求职者需要更多策略和外部帮助。
• 反馈机制的缺失：susiecambria强调了求职反馈的重要性，而其他评论者则没有提到这一点，显示出反馈机制在求职过程中的稀缺性。
• 人际关系和内部推荐：Spivak和Noumenon72提到通过人际网络获得求职机会的重要性，这与单纯依赖网上申请表形成对比。
• 教育与市场需求脱节：gngoo对CS教育无法跟上行业变化表示担忧，并质疑初级职位的存在和求职者的竞争力。

争议焦点：当前求职难度是否被夸大，以及求职失败的原因是否仅归因于市场变化和教育脱节，还是与求职者自身条件（如学历、简历质量、项目经验）有关。

data.title: Fortescue Infinity Train electric locomotive never needs fuel or charging
data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary: Fortescue has unveiled its "Infinity Train," a battery-electric locomotive prototype, marking a significant step toward decarbonizing its mining operations. The train, developed with Downer Group, uses regenerative braking and gravitational energy during downhill trips to recharge its batteries, eliminating the need for external charging or fuel. On its 1,100 km journey from Perth to the Pilbara, the train demonstrated its capability to handle heavy haulage without fossil fuels, potentially saving 82 million liters of diesel annually and reducing Fortescue's carbon emissions by 235,200 tons. This innovation supports the company's goal of achieving "Real Zero" emissions.

44339903.article_content:

Fortescue Infinity Train electric locomotive never needs fuel or charging
Jo Borrás
| Jun 21 2025 - 11:46 am PT
13 Comments
Fortescue has taken the wraps off a prototype of its proposed “Infinity Train” electric locomotive, making the 1,100 km (about 685 miles) trip from Perth to the Pilbara and marking a major milestone in the decarbonization of the company’s heavy haul operations.
Co-developed with the locomotive experts at Downer Group,
Fortescue
revealed its concept for a battery electric “Infinity Train”
back in March of 2022
. At the time, the company promised a “world’s first” iron ore train capable of fully charging its batteries through regenerative braking. The two companies claimed the clever technology would create a self-sustaining, zero-emission rail system powered entirely by the force of gravity during the train’s loaded downhill travels.
This week, the concept went from the drawing board to the real world, completing an 1,100 km trip across Australia and proving itself to be up to the task of handling the grueling demands of Fortescue’s massive mining operations.
“We’re thrilled to see our battery electric locomotive prototype arrive in the Pilbara,” said
Ellie Coates, CEO of Fortescue Zero. She added that the achievement, using zero fossil fuels, “represent(s) a major step in Fortescue’s journey to Real Zero.”
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The Fortescue Infinity Train uses the energy produced by slowing the loaded train on downhill sections of the company’s 385 mile private, heavy-haul rail network to recharge its battery systems. That energy is enough to bring the unloaded train back to the mine, eliminating the need for external charging infrastructure or additional renewable energy sources, making the train almost entirely self-sufficient.
Fortescue says the deployment of the Infinity Train concept at its mines will eliminate more than 82 million liters of diesel fuel consumption (about 21 million gallons, which ChatGPT tells me amounts to about 235,200 tons of CO₂ emissions).
That change alone would eliminate about 11% of Scope 1 emissions annually for Fortescue all on its own,
putting it well on its way to its stated goal of achieving “Real Zero” emissions-free operations
.
Electrek’s Take
Infinity Train on the rails; via Fortescue.
Using gravity to charge up heavily-laden mining vehicles on downhill runs is an idea that’s been put into practice for years
, with great success wherever the topography allows (
since 2017
, at least). Combining that clever use of gravity, traction braking, and battery storage for use on a rail system like this just seems smart, and it makes me think we’re just scratching the surface of all the clever ways electrification and battery storage will eventually get put to use.
I wonder what would happen if you threw some battery electric rail cars into the mix
, as well!? You guys are smart, head down to the comments and let me know (and, while you’re there, help me check ChatGPT’s math on those carbon emissions).

data.title: Klong: A Simple Array Language
data.author: tosh
data.article_summary: Klong是一种类似于K语言的数组语言，但更加明确清晰。它主要用于操作列表和多维数组，采用数学符号进行编程。Klong程序由一组函数构成，使用预定义的操作符来处理数据。例如，判断一个数是否为质数的程序为：`{&/x!:\2+!_x^1%2}`。对于不熟悉数组语言的用户，Klong可能会比较复杂且具有挑战性。文档包括参考手册、入门书籍和快速参考，帮助用户学习与使用Klong。Klong使用ANSI C编写，可以在多种系统上编译安装，并且有一个名为KlongPy的加速版本可供选择。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：数组编程语言（如Klong等）的可读性、实用性及其与其他编程范式的对比

不同观点：
• why218：认为批评数组语言不可读的人是没有意识到这种风格可能带来的积极权衡。他将数组编程比作用符号进行数学运算，认为这种编程风格可以让程序员更快地思考和处理复杂问题。不过他承认这种风格并不适合所有人，且学习时间可能不值得。
• Duanemclemore：分享了自己选择Dyalog APL而非Klong的经历，但认为熟悉数组范式的人会觉得Klong简单直观。同时，提到Klong在Array Cast播客中被提及，并表达对某些类型节目的喜爱。
• Aken：认为数组语言可能对一些人来说难以理解，但对自己不成问题。通过一个简短的程序示例展示了Klong的简洁性，但也表现出对其可读性的调侃。
• cosmic_quanta：承认数组技术在特定领域有价值，但认为其符号过于简练，学习成本高，且质疑选择Klong而非Futhark或Accelerate的理由。
• haolez：猜测极度简洁的语言可能会因LLMs（大型语言模型）而受欢迎，因为它们节省 tokens，但训练数据不如JavaScript全面。
• nils-m-holm：回应关于Klong和Lisp的问题，指出Klong数组和Lisp的S表达式在实现上非常相似，甚至可以用LISP函数和宏来实现Klong。
• etbebl：质疑数组语言用户与使用MATLAB、Numpy、Julia等科学计算语言的用户之间的重叠性，认为后者更倾向于使用熟悉的函数调用而非学习新的书写系统。
• ljouhet：提到对Klong中的monad理解困难，表现出对某些概念复杂性的困惑。
• emorning3：直接提问Klong数组和Lisp的S表达式有何不同，显示出对两者区别的求知欲。
• thomasmg：认为尝试使用数组语言只会让人沮丧，表现出对这种语言的抗拒。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：数组语言的可读性与学习成本。why218等人认为这种语言风格有其优势，而cosmic_quanta和thomasmg等人则认为学习成本高且不值得。
• 其他值得注意的讨论点：数组语言在LLMs中的潜在应用（haolez），以及与其他编程范式（如Lisp和科学计算语言）的比较（nils-m-holm, etbebl）。
• 用户背景和经验：不同用户对数组语言的理解和接受程度各异，Aken和Duanemclemore表现出对这种语言的适应性，而ljouhet和thomasmg则表现出困惑和抗拒。

/   (

|

Klong
A Simple Array Language
The Klong Book
Documentation
|
Download
Klong is an array language, like K, but without the
ambiguity
. If
you know K or APL, you may be disappointed by Klong. If you don't
know any array languages, it might explode your brain. Use at your
own risk!
Programming in Klong
A Klong program is a set of functions that use various pre-defined
operators to manipulate lists (vectors) and (multi-dimensional)
arrays. Here is a program that checks whether a number
x
is prime
(for
x>2
):
{&/x!:\2+!_x^1%2}
Note that Klong is a mathematical notation rather than a programming
language. If you try to use it like your favorite functional/procedural/OO
programming language, you will only get frustrated. Here's an
explanation of the above program
.
Learn More About Klong
The Reference Manual (
klong-ref.txt
) provides a complete and detailed
semi-formal description of the Klong language. It is probably the
best starting point for exploring Klong.
An Introduction to Array Programming in Klong
is a book
that offers a detailed explanation of problem solving in Klong and
array languages in general.
The Quick Reference (
klong-qref.txt
) summarizes the syntax and
semantics of the language. It will probably only make sense if you
already know K or APL.
Then there is a Really Short Introduction to Klong (
klong-intro.txt
),
which you might want to read if you have never used an array language
before.
Finally, if you already know K, here is a (probably incomplete)
summary of differences between Klong and K:
klong-vs-k.txt
.
Compiling and Installing Klong
You can download Klong here:
klong20221212.tgz
(~170KB, recent changes).
Just in case, here are the previous stable versions:
klong20190926.tgz
(~156KB),
klong20171119.tgz
(~120KB, old syntax).
Klong is written in pure ANSI C (C99), so it should compile on any
system providing a C compiler. Just run make and make test. It also
compiles natively on Plan 9!
To install Klong, just copy the
kg
binary to
/usr/local/bin
or some
similar place and point the
KLONGPATH
environment variable to the
lib/
directory of the Klong source tree.
Files ending in
.kg
are Klong programs, you can load them with
]lname
or
./kg -l name
(with or without the suffix).
Good luck!
KlongPy
In case my Klong interpreter is not fast enough for you, Brian
Gurraci has created a vectorized version of Klong named KlongPy.
You can find it on GitHub:
https://github.com/briangu/klongpy

data.title: Oklo, the Earth's Two-billion-year-old only Known Natural Nuclear Reactor (2018)
data.author: keepamovin
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了地球上已知的唯一天然核反应堆——奥克洛（Oklo）的发现和意义。1972年，物理学家弗朗西斯·佩林在法国一家核燃料处理厂发现，从非洲加蓬一个矿场提取的铀矿样本中铀-235（U-235）的比例异常偏低，只有0.717%，而正常情况下应为0.720%。这一发现引发了研究人员的关注，最终确认奥克洛是一个天然核反应堆，约在20亿年前自发进行了核链式反应。这一现象帮助科学家更好地理解核反应过程以及铀在自然界中的行为。奥克洛样本还被捐赠给了维也纳的自然历史博物馆。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于非洲奥克洛地区天然核反应堆的历史、科学意义及其引发的讨论。

不同观点：
• **b800h的观点**：介绍了奥克洛地区的天然核反应堆，发生在约17亿至18亿年前，持续了几十万年，平均热功率小于100千瓦。这一现象是由于特殊的地质条件使铀-235达到临界状态，并通过自然水作为中子减速剂。

• **legitster的观点**：引用Richard Rhodes的观点，指出这一天然核反应堆为批评者提供了一个反驳的例子，证明核废料可以通过埋藏安全处置，且能长时间保持稳定。

• **wjnc的观点**：对文章的信息量不足表示失望，提出了一系列关于反应规模、能量释放、时间跨度及可见性等问题。并通过Claude和Wikipedia获取补充信息，确认了反应堆平均热功率为100千瓦。

• **foobarian的观点**：讨论了奥克洛铀矿中铀-235的含量微小差异，引发了对测量误差范围的兴趣，并幽默地表示如果是垃圾软件开发者可能会忽视这种微小差异。

• **Aardwolf的观点**：进一步探讨了天然铀中铀-235含量的普遍性，提出了是否与太阳系形成时的超新星爆炸有关，并进一步思考银河系其他部分或外来物质对地球的影响。

补充讨论：
• **kkwteh的观点**：半开玩笑地提出奥克洛的天然核反应堆可能是古代文明或核战争的遗迹。

• **stmw的观点**：提到了一家名为Oklo的创业公司，该公司制造被动安全的核反应堆，将历史与现代科技联系起来。

• **HelloUsername的观点**：提供了一个2018年的相关链接，引导读者查看更多讨论。

• **eabeezxjc的观点**：附和kkwteh的观点，认为可能是动荡时期核战争的遗迹。

• **fnord77的观点**：提出一个有趣的问题，即奥克洛是已知的唯一天然核反应堆，而恒星是否也可以被视为天然核反应堆。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在奥克洛现象的科学意义及其对现代核废料处理的启示。一些人认为这是核废料可以安全埋藏的证据，而另一些人则关注信息不足，希望了解更多具体数据和背景信息。

• 对天然铀中铀-235含量微小差异的测量误差及其可能的宇宙学意义存在讨论。

• 半开玩笑的古代文明或核战争遗迹的猜测引发了轻松的讨论，但并未被严肃对待。

Samples of Oklo donated to Vienna's Natural History Museum. (Photo: Ludovic Ferrière/Natural  History Museum)
Physicist Francis Perrin sat at a nuclearfuel-processing plant down in the south of France, thinking to himself: “This cannot be possible.” It was 1972. On the one hand, there was a dark piece of radioactive natural uranium ore, extracted from a mine in Africa. On the other, accepted scientific data about the constant ratio of radioactive uranium in ore.
Examination of this high-grade ore from a mine in Gabon was found to contain a lower proportion of uranium-235 (U-235) — the fissile sort. Only a tiny bit less, but enough to make the researchers sit back and scratch their heads.
The physicists’ first, logical response to such an unusual ratio of U-235 was that this was not natural uranium. All natural uranium today contains 0.720% of U-235. If you were to extract it from the Earth’s crust, or from rocks from the moon or in meteorites, that’s what you would find. But that bit of rock from Oklo contained only 0.717%.

44326145.article_summary: 本文介绍了地球上已知的唯一天然核反应堆——奥克洛（Oklo）的发现和意义。1972年，物理学家弗朗西斯·佩林在法国一家核燃料处理厂发现，从非洲加蓬一个矿场提取的铀矿样本中铀-235（U-235）的比例异常偏低，只有0.717%，而正常情况下应为0.720%。这一发现引发了研究人员的关注，最终确认奥克洛是一个天然核反应堆，约在20亿年前自发进行了核链式反应。这一现象帮助科学家更好地理解核反应过程以及铀在自然界中的行为。奥克洛样本还被捐赠给了维也纳的自然历史博物馆。
44326145.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于非洲奥克洛地区天然核反应堆的历史、科学意义及其引发的讨论。

不同观点：
• **b800h的观点**：介绍了奥克洛地区的天然核反应堆，发生在约17亿至18亿年前，持续了几十万年，平均热功率小于100千瓦。这一现象是由于特殊的地质条件使铀-235达到临界状态，并通过自然水作为中子减速剂。

• **legitster的观点**：引用Richard Rhodes的观点，指出这一天然核反应堆为批评者提供了一个反驳的例子，证明核废料可以通过埋藏安全处置，且能长时间保持稳定。

• **wjnc的观点**：对文章的信息量不足表示失望，提出了一系列关于反应规模、能量释放、时间跨度及可见性等问题。并通过Claude和Wikipedia获取补充信息，确认了反应堆平均热功率为100千瓦。

• **foobarian的观点**：讨论了奥克洛铀矿中铀-235的含量微小差异，引发了对测量误差范围的兴趣，并幽默地表示如果是垃圾软件开发者可能会忽视这种微小差异。

• **Aardwolf的观点**：进一步探讨了天然铀中铀-235含量的普遍性，提出了是否与太阳系形成时的超新星爆炸有关，并进一步思考银河系其他部分或外来物质对地球的影响。

补充讨论：
• **kkwteh的观点**：半开玩笑地提出奥克洛的天然核反应堆可能是古代文明或核战争的遗迹。

• **stmw的观点**：提到了一家名为Oklo的创业公司，该公司制造被动安全的核反应堆，将历史与现代科技联系起来。

• **HelloUsername的观点**：提供了一个2018年的相关链接，引导读者查看更多讨论。

• **eabeezxjc的观点**：附和kkwteh的观点，认为可能是动荡时期核战争的遗迹。

• **fnord77的观点**：提出一个有趣的问题，即奥克洛是已知的唯一天然核反应堆，而恒星是否也可以被视为天然核反应堆。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在奥克洛现象的科学意义及其对现代核废料处理的启示。一些人认为这是核废料可以安全埋藏的证据，而另一些人则关注信息不足，希望了解更多具体数据和背景信息。

• 对天然铀中铀-235含量微小差异的测量误差及其可能的宇宙学意义存在讨论。

• 半开玩笑的古代文明或核战争遗迹的猜测引发了轻松的讨论，但并未被严肃对待。

data.title: Apple typewriter memo (2020)
data.author: rafaepta
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要介绍了苹果公司早期CEO Mike Scott的职业生涯及其影响，包括他试图终止Macintosh项目和在“黑色星期三”解雇40名员工的举动，之后他自己也被解雇。Scott后来成为宝石专家，一种矿物以他的名字命名。文章提到Scott的一份备忘录，通过纸质形式分发，可能使用Apple II打印，并指出备忘录中有拼写错误。文中还讨论了备忘录中提到的"Ken"可能是谁，以及当时使用的文字处理设备，如Digital Equipment Corporation的字处理器和Apple II的Apple Writer系统。文章最后提到，尽管技术进步，打字机仍未完全被淘汰，某些老式打字机仍在使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对技术设备（如打字机、文字处理器等）的使用体验和历史演变的不同看法

不同观点：
• yosef123：认为公司禁止打字机的举动并不负面，反而表明公司对其产品有信心，并可能希望改进产品。他指出，当产品不被其创造者使用时，用户体验往往不好。

• squelchy5000：批评文字处理器的设计不够人性化，特别是长文档处理时，用户需要从上到下滚动，而不是让文本自动上滚，这与打字机相比失去了某些优点。

• PaulHoule：分享了个人经历，讲述了早期的计算机设备如PDP-8/A和VT-61终端的使用体验，以及这些设备在特定场景（如小报社的排版）中的应用。他认为尽管Apple ][+在某些方面优于PDP-8/A，但PDP-8/A的终端具有80列显示的优势。

• mproud：认为讨论中的文章具有讽刺意味，目的更多是为了幽默，而不是严肃的讨论。他指出，文章表面上是在推崇打字机，实际上却是在Apple产品上写的，带有调侃性质。

• ginko：对打字机是否过时提出质疑，认为打字机在自己的专业领域中已经很少见，并表示对打字机的使用感到陌生。

补充讨论：
• 不同用户对打字机和现代文字处理器的实用性有不同看法。squelchy5000和ginko认为打字机已经过时或不如现代设备好用，而yosef123和PaulHoule则在某种程度上认可打字机或早期计算设备的历史价值和特定场景下的优势。

• 争议焦点在于打字机是否真的过时以及现代文字处理器的设计是否充分考虑了用户体验。squelchy5000对现代处理器的设计提出了具体批评，而ginko则质疑打字机在当代的实际应用价值。

• mproud强调了文章的幽默性质，提醒读者不要过于认真对待讨论内容，这也为整个讨论增加了一层轻松的氛围。

44340790.article_content:
.
.. and typewriters
still
aren't obsolete!
A few memos about the memo:
•
Mike Scott
served as the first CEO of Apple, from February 1977 to March 1981. His other fine judgments include trying to shut down the Macintosh project and firing 40 employees on so-called "Black Wednesday," a move that he claimed would make the company "fun" again. He himself was fired as CEO shortly thereafter. However, "Scotty" has enjoyed a brilliant later career as an
expert on gemstones
. The mineral
Scottyite
, a barium copper silicate, was named in his honor.
• Scotty's memo evidently was distributed on paper, using a pre-printed form. I assume it was typed on an Apple II, but I am not sure. Apparently his writing device didn't have spell-check (note the misspelling "priorty" and the three spaces between "and" and "convince").
• It's possible that "Ken" was
Ken Rothmuller
, who was the Lisa project manager at the time. But Mr. Rothmuller tells me that he doesn't recall the memo or using a DEC word processor, and that most of the Lisa team would have been using the Apple II for writing.  He is not aware of another Ken working at Apple in 1980, but it's possible that there was a Ken in the main building; the Lisa team worked in a different building. Mr. Rothmuller adds that although Scott was the CEO, Steve Jobs was actually making a lot of the decisions.
• Ken's Digital Equipment Corporation word processor probably looked something like this (
source
). (In the early '60s, DEC had developed one of the first word-processing programs, humorously called
Expensive Typewriter
.)
• "Apple II-Apple Writer Systems":
Apple Writer
(1979) was a word-processing application for the Apple II computer. It displayed text only in uppercase, though capitalized letters could be highlighted. What a beautiful advancement over typewriters, eh?
• "Apple high performance systems" just seems to be a general category that makes a vague promise about future advancements.
• Scott's phrase "direct typing capabilities" doesn't seem to exist anywhere outside this memo, but I think he meant the ability to type immediately onto paper, with no word processing intervening between the keyboard and the printing.
•
Qume
was a leading manufacturer of daisy-wheel printers. Did "Qume with Keyboard/Apple installations" mean a setup that allowed the Qume printer to function like a typewriter (immediately printing when you hit a key)? Qume did produce some computer monitors and keyboards at some point in the '80s, but I imagine Apple wouldn't be using those.
Four decades later, what has happened? Apple, of course, successfully developed the Mac, and found new prosperity and influence in the 21st century thanks to the iPod, iPad, and iPhone. There is an
Apple II aficionado group on Facebook
with over 7000 members. Typewriters have been relegated to the margins of business, but many businesses still keep one around. Electronic and manual typewriters are still manufactured. And the great, durable mid-20th-century typewriters are still clacking away....

data.title: Maple Mono: open-source monospace font with round corner
data.author: Bluestein
data.article_summary: Maple Mono是一款开源的圆角等宽字体，专为编程设计，支持连字和控制台图标，具有细粒度的自定义选项。该字体提供可变的字重和斜体字形，中英文宽度比例为2:1，适合多语言显示和Markdown表格。它支持Nerd-Font，使终端更生动，并针对IDE和终端进行了优化。用户可以通过多种包管理器如Scoop、Homebrew和ArchLinuxCN安装不同版本的Maple Mono，包括中文版（CN）和常规版。该字体在GitHub上获得了17.3k星标和561次 fork，具有广泛的社区支持。

Maple Mono
Maple Mono is an open source monospace font focused on smoothing your coding flow.
I create it to enhance my working experience, and hope that it can be useful to others.
V7 is a completely remade version, providing variable font format and source files of font project, redesigning more than half of the glyphs and offering smarter ligatures. You can checkout V6
here
Features
✨ Variable - Infinity font weights with fine-grained italic glyphs.
☁️ Smooth - Round corner, brand-new glyph of
@ $ % & Q ->
and cursive
f i j k l x y
in italic style.
💪 Useful - Large amount of smart ligatures, see in
features/
🎨 Icon - First-Class
Nerd-Font
support, make your terminal more vivid.
🔨 Customize - Enable or disable font features as you want, just make your own font.
Simpified Chinese, Traditional Chinese and Japanese
CN version based on
Resource Han Rounded
provides complete character set support for Chinese development environments, including Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, and Japanese. Meanwhile, the characteristic of perfect 2:1 alignment between Chinese and English allows this font to achieve a neat, uniform, beautiful, and comfortable appearance in scenarios such as multilingual display and Markdown tables. However, the spacing of Chinese characters is larger compared to other popular Chinese fonts. See details in
release notes
and
this issue
.

主要讨论点：围绕机器人技术及其历史、应用、技术挑战等展开的讨论

不同观点：
• [Symmetry] 认为文章遗漏了一个重要事件，即Boston Dynamics的机器人被枪击的事件，并提供了相关新闻链接。此外，他还补充了一个关于编程语言启发的链接，为文章提供了背景信息。
• [z3ratul163071] 对文章中提到的ROS操作系统发表评论，认为文章隐藏了一个有趣的点，即ROS虽然被广泛使用，但一些公司和研究人员难以从该系统迁移出去。
• [modeless] 讨论了Google在机器人领域的收购及其后续发展，认为Google在解雇Andy Rubin后失去了对机器人项目的耐心，导致项目停滞并最终被出售给SoftBank。他认为高层管理支持的缺乏是失败的原因。
• [nsxwolf] 对文章标题表示质疑，不确定这篇文章是否是某种形式的“如何避免”指南，显示出对文章实际内容的困惑。
• [ianbicking] 提出了关于远程临场技术为何没有普及的问题，引发对技术应用场景的讨论。
• [degrees57] 分享了个人经历，提到Odetics的Odex 1机器人，并描述了其参与的一个展示活动，补充了文章未涉及的历史细节。
• [mooseling] 表达了在情感低谷时对类似文章的喜爱，并请求更多类似内容推荐，显示出对轻松且易于理解的技术文章的需求。
• [smath] 提出了一个技术性问题，询问让机器人叠衣服或洗碗的最佳方法，显示出对具体机器人应用的关注。
• [outside1234] 以幽默的方式评论了Tesla的Optimus机器人部署情况，暗示其高成本和低效率的问题，批评了其实际应用价值。
• [taneq] 对文章中的幽默和回溯性定义（如AI的滑稽反义解释）表示欣赏，提出了对AI定义变化的思考。
• [gdiamos] 质疑文章是否由ChatGPT生成，反映了当前对AI生成内容的关注和讨论。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是Google在机器人项目上的管理和决策，特别是解雇Andy Rubin对项目的影响。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是对ROS操作系统在研究和商业应用中的实际挑战，以及其广泛使用和难以迁移的问题。
• 评论中还涉及了对具体机器人应用（如远程临场、家务机器人）的兴趣和疑问，显示出对技术实际应用的关注。
• 幽默和个人故事在评论中也扮演了重要角色，反映出读者对轻松且具有人情味的内容的偏好。

data.title: The Tangled Past and Unsettled Future of Greyhound Racing in West Virginia
data.author: gmays
data.article_summary: 《在西弗吉尼亚，灰狗赛跑的复杂历史与不确定未来》一文探讨了美国最后一个活跃的灰狗赛道所在的州，传统与不确定性并存。文章描述了赛狗的古老渊源，它们曾被多个古代文明所喜爱，因其高贵和狩猎能力而备受珍视。然而，如今的赛狗行业在西弗吉尼亚州面临衰退。文章提到，尽管观看赛狗的人数大幅减少，根据州规定，赛道每年仍需举办至少200天比赛。自佛罗里达州在2019年禁止赛狗以来，西弗吉尼亚的赛狗业更加萧条。文章质疑，既然赛狗不再为公司带来可观收入，为何它们仍在奔跑？这涉及赌博合法化的历史和社会许可的变化。灰狗赛跑曾是非法活动，但在大萧条时期被合法化，尽管面临道德和动物福利方面的反对。如今，这一行业面临存续问题，反映了其社会和经济合法性的逐渐丧失。

Two greyhounds at night
, 2019, oil on panel by Clare Menck © The artist. Courtesy 99 Loop Gallery
Issue 129, Summer 2025
May 23, 2025
The Tangled Past and Unsettled Future of Greyhound Racing in West Virginia
In the home of America’s last active tracks, tradition and uncertainty run neck and neck
By Michelle Orange
This story appears in the Summer 2025 print edition with the title “Comely in Going.
” O
rder the Y’all Street Issue
here
.
T
hey look ancient because they are.
Eight in all, each one led by a teenaged handler in a royal purple t-shirt, the dogs cut a silhouette at odds with their surroundings. Moving from the paddock to the gated starting blocks, they squat and sniff and occasionally bark, appearing most themselves, or most familiar, when flattened in profile: the elegant, tapered snout, stretched-out torso, and tiny waist; the massive haunches and sickle-shaped curve of the belly. The same stark, primeval outlines can be found in Roman mosaics and temple drawings dating back to 6000 BC. The Greeks, the Celts, the Egyptians—they all loved the greyhound, or its close relations. Bred and cherished for its perceived nobility as much as its hunting prowess, no dog has been depicted as frequently, across as many millennia, or by a broader range of humans.
Signs of that linkage are scarce on an August afternoon in Wheeling, West Virginia, home to one of this country’s two remaining active greyhound racetracks. Yet despite the shambling, urine-soaked starting-block procession and barren, unsplendid backdrop, there persists a sense of something wondrous happening, of watching eight walking hieroglyphs pass by.
Earlier, inside the viewing bay—an eerily quiet, glass-enclosed grandstand where roughly two dozen people sat hunched, in clusters and alone, marking their betting sheets and sampling concessions—I stood with Kim Florence, the president and general manager of Wheeling Island Hotel, Casino & Racetrack, and Glen White, a representative of Delaware North, the resort’s Buffalo-based parent company. There, we passed the last ten minutes of our hour together pointedly not talking about the thing we were there to talk about. Behind us, a handful of old men sat facing a wall of television screens simulcasting horse races from around the country. Below us, a tomato-red dirt Zamboni groomed the 548-yard track during the eleven-minute break before the next of the afternoon’s eighteen greyhound races, each of which lasts about thirty seconds.
If these dogs are no longer driving company revenue, why are they still running?
Time was, even ten or fifteen years ago, Wheeling Island ran thirty races a day. By state mandate, they must hold live races on no fewer than two hundred days each year. Since 2019, the year after Florida voters approved an amendment to ban greyhound racing at the eleven remaining tracks in that state, the already diminished number of racing patrons at Wheeling Island has declined by more than half. These numbers are not the stuff of happy executives, or budget meetings. Florence and White had agreed to meet with me but asked that the details of our conversation be off the record. Our tour of the facility included a stop inside the track kennel, where 144 dogs made a proportional racket from within their stacked wire enclosures, and the adjoining adoption kennel, where eighteen former racers snoozed in individual stalls behind a purple velvet curtain. Meant to showcase the track’s orderly and humane operation, the tour had also circled, in purely corporate terms, the question at hand: If these dogs are no longer driving company revenue, why are they still running?
T
he answer requires an unfolding of the origami compact by which certain pursuits gain and lose legitimacy—acquiring social and legal licenses and then, less often, especially if they are profitable, having one or both licenses taken away. The history of wagering in the U.S. is one such compact: Once the purview of gangsters and their prey, gambling in some form is now legal, and indeed a source of government revenue, in all but two states. The history of greyhound racing is another: By 1930, ten years after a man named Owen Patrick Smith opened the first commercially recognized greyhound track in the country, in Emeryville, California, there were sixty-seven such tracks in operation—all of them illegal. Five years after that, Depression-era economics had changed the political calculus: Florida, Oregon, and Massachusetts had all legalized dog racing; twenty more states were to follow, despite moral and personal objections voiced by various legislators, church groups, and animal welfare organizations along the way. Though dog racing lacked the glamour and prestige of horse racing and never became as popular, greyhounds were easier to breed and less expensive to keep. They were also an exotic concern: The first greyhound was registered in the U.S. in 1894, and relatively few Americans kept them for hunting or as pets. Trained using

data.title: Minimal auto-differentiation engine in Rust
data.author: lschneider
data.article_summary: **nanograd** 是一个用Rust编写的最小自动微分引擎。它通过定义 `Scalar` 结构体来实现，每个 `Scalar` 存储值、可选的梯度以及生成它的操作描述。通过操作符重载（如 `+`、`*`、`-` 等）和 `scalar::func` 中的辅助函数，构建出一个由 `Scalar` 节点组成的有向无环图（DAG）。调用 `backward()` 方法可以从输出节点开始递归地传播梯度，并累积到通过 `Scalar::new_grad` 创建的叶子节点中。该项目包含一个训练小型多层感知机（MLP）学习XOR功能的演示，并能通过 `plot::dump_graph` 将计算图可视化为一个包含D3.js的HTML文件。项目使用MIT许可证，目前获得44个星标。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于自动微分中全局/共享状态的改变及其潜在问题，以及对项目设计和实现的讨论

不同观点：
• **amelius的观点**：提出关于全局/共享状态的改变可能会导致问题。具体来说，当多个函数同时进行反向传播（backward pass），并且这些函数依赖于相同的变量（如x和y）时，收集这些变量的偏导数（partial derivatives）可能会出现冲突。amelius认为更好的设计是使用z.get_grad(x)和w.get_grad(x)这种方式，分别获取每个函数对变量的偏导数，而不是直接通过x.get_grad()这种共享方式。

• **tnlogy的观点**：对项目表示赞赏，并分享了自己曾经做过的一个类似的小项目，目的是学习Rust和复习机器学习知识。虽然最初计划将计算图存储在堆中以便后续发送到GPU上执行，但因为某些原因（如懒惰）而放弃了该计划。tnlogy强调，即使项目未完成，也能从中学习到东西。

• **kragen的观点**：认为在标题中加入"backward-mode"（反向模式）会更有助于理解。这个观点主要是针对文档或项目命名提出的小建议，旨在让读者更容易明白项目涉及的核心概念。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于共享状态在多线程环境下的安全性，amelius认为直接使用共享变量收集偏导数可能导致错误结果，而未直接提出解决方案，只是建议通过更明确的方式获取每个函数的偏导数。
• tnlogy的评论更多是个人经验分享，没有直接参与到技术争议中，但提供了实践中的心得。
• kragen的评论则是对项目文档的命名提出改进建议，未涉及技术细节争议。

How it works
Each
Scalar
stores
value
, optional
gradient
, and an
Edge
describing the operation that produced it.
Operator overloads (
+
,
*
,
-
, ...) and helpers in
scalar::func
build a directed acyclic graph of
Scalar
s while caching the
local derivative
for every edge.
backward()
starts at an output node and
recursively propagates gradients
along the graph, accumulating them into the leaf nodes created with
Scalar::new_grad
.
The graph can be visualised with
plot::dump_graph
, which emits a self-contained D3.js HTML file.

44327759.article_summary: **nanograd** 是一个用Rust编写的最小自动微分引擎。它通过定义 `Scalar` 结构体来实现，每个 `Scalar` 存储值、可选的梯度以及生成它的操作描述。通过操作符重载（如 `+`、`*`、`-` 等）和 `scalar::func` 中的辅助函数，构建出一个由 `Scalar` 节点组成的有向无环图（DAG）。调用 `backward()` 方法可以从输出节点开始递归地传播梯度，并累积到通过 `Scalar::new_grad` 创建的叶子节点中。该项目包含一个训练小型多层感知机（MLP）学习XOR功能的演示，并能通过 `plot::dump_graph` 将计算图可视化为一个包含D3.js的HTML文件。项目使用MIT许可证，目前获得44个星标。
44327759.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于自动微分中全局/共享状态的改变及其潜在问题，以及对项目设计和实现的讨论

不同观点：
• **amelius的观点**：提出关于全局/共享状态的改变可能会导致问题。具体来说，当多个函数同时进行反向传播（backward pass），并且这些函数依赖于相同的变量（如x和y）时，收集这些变量的偏导数（partial derivatives）可能会出现冲突。amelius认为更好的设计是使用z.get_grad(x)和w.get_grad(x)这种方式，分别获取每个函数对变量的偏导数，而不是直接通过x.get_grad()这种共享方式。

• **tnlogy的观点**：对项目表示赞赏，并分享了自己曾经做过的一个类似的小项目，目的是学习Rust和复习机器学习知识。虽然最初计划将计算图存储在堆中以便后续发送到GPU上执行，但因为某些原因（如懒惰）而放弃了该计划。tnlogy强调，即使项目未完成，也能从中学习到东西。

• **kragen的观点**：认为在标题中加入"backward-mode"（反向模式）会更有助于理解。这个观点主要是针对文档或项目命名提出的小建议，旨在让读者更容易明白项目涉及的核心概念。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于共享状态在多线程环境下的安全性，amelius认为直接使用共享变量收集偏导数可能导致错误结果，而未直接提出解决方案，只是建议通过更明确的方式获取每个函数的偏导数。
• tnlogy的评论更多是个人经验分享，没有直接参与到技术争议中，但提供了实践中的心得。
• kragen的评论则是对项目文档的命名提出改进建议，未涉及技术细节争议。

data.author: busymom0
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源代码的价值与风险，特别是在生成式AI（如LLM）时代下的影响。

不同观点：
• **marssaxman的观点**：支持开源，认为自己的代码无论是直接还是间接被使用都不重要，关键是希望别人能用。
• **Viliam1234的观点**：也支持开源，认为自己从别人那里学到了很多，开源是一种回馈方式。
• **ipaddr的观点**：对开源持怀疑态度。担心在当前LLM生成辅助的背景下，开源项目可能会被他人利用，甚至冒名顶替，从而让原创工作贬值。认为代码的价值正在被削弱。
• **msgodel的观点**：认为ipaddr的观点近乎疯狂，似乎不认同对开源持如此消极的态度。
• **danjl的观点**：对开源持积极态度，认为即便LLM从开源代码中学习并改进，最终也会帮助所有人。提到自己写的大量代码已经消失在历史中，希望它们能被保存下来。
• **throwarayes的观点**：认为即使LLM利用开源代码，也需要付出维护和再创造的努力，门槛较高。对于使用Apache/MIT许可的开源代码，不介意他人从中获取片段。
• **chistev的观点**：对开源持犹豫态度，担心自己正在开发的SAAS项目未来可能盈利。不过也提到如果项目失败，会考虑将其开源以丰富个人作品集。
• **RicoElectrico的观点**：从艺术家角度分析，认为代码和艺术作品一样，其价值主要在于知识和经验。提到历史上创作和复制的难易程度变化，指出在AI时代，创作变得容易，传统创作者谋生的模式受到挑战。
• **bigyabai的观点**：认为代码没有内在价值，除非他人逐字复制并违反许可，否则不算“剽窃”。不担心AI时代下的开源，引用Stallman的观点，认为代码的最大价值在于对他人有实用性，并支持零利润开源软件生产作为最终目标。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：开源代码在AI时代的价值和风险，尤其是LLM可能利用开源代码生成新项目，导致原创作者被忽视或冒名。部分人认为代码的价值在于知识和经验的积累，而另一些人则认为代码应更多地服务于公共利益，即便在AI时代也是如此。
• **对AI影响的看法分歧**：一些人担心AI会削弱代码的独特性和原创性，而另一些人则认为AI能帮助改进代码并造福所有人。
• **开源许可的角色**：讨论中多次提到开源许可的重要性，如Apache/MIT许可，认为这些许可在保护原创作者权益的同时，也促进了代码的共享和使用。

data.title: Sound As Pure Form: Music Language Inspired by Supercollider, APL, and Forth
data.author: mindcrime
data.article_summary: "Sound As Pure Form" (sapf) 是一个用于音频合成的解释器，采用类似Forth的语法，支持懒惰列表和类似APL的自动映射。该语言功能性强、基于栈、使用后缀表示法，旨在通过高层次的函数和自动映射、扫描、归约操作符处理音频和控制事件。sapf受APL、Joy、Haskell等语言启发，强调简洁表达和并发处理能力。其特点包括函数组合自然、无需考虑操作优先级和分隔符、支持多返回值等。虽然受启于连接式编程，但sapf包含词法变量。设置包括将程序放入执行路径、去除苹果的隔离属性、配置环境变量，并可通过命令行运行和查看示例。

WHAT
This program is called:
"A tool for exploring sound as pure form." or "sound as pure form" or "sapf"
It is an interpreter for a language for creating and transforming sound. The
language is mostly functional, stack based and uses postfix notation similar to
FORTH. It represents audio and control events using lazy, possibly infinite
sequences. It intends to do for lazy sequences what APL does for arrays: provide
very high level functions with pervasive automatic mapping, scanning, and
reduction operators. This makes for a language where short programs can achieve
results out of proportion to their size. Because nearly all of the programmer
accessible data types are immutable, the language can easily run multiple
threads without deadlock or corruption.
WHY
Other languages that inspired this one:
APL, Joy[1], Haskell, Piccola[2], Nyquist[3], SuperCollider[4].
APL and FORTH (from which Joy derives) are both widely derided for being
write-only languages. Nevertheless, there has yet to be a language of such
concise expressive power as APL or its descendants. APL is powerful not because
of its bizarre symbols or syntax, but due to the way it automatically maps
operations over arrays and allows iterations at depth within arrays. This means
one almost never needs to write a loop or think about operations one-at-a-time.
Instead one can think about operations on whole structures.
Here is a great quote from Alan Perlis[5] on APL, which that also reflects my
interest in this way of programming :
"What attracted me, then, to APL was a feeling that perhaps through APL one
might begin to acquire some of the dimensions in programming that we revere in
natural language — some of the pleasures of composition; of saying things
elegantly; of being brief, poetic, artistic, that makes our natural languages
so precious to us."
The Joy language introduced concatenative functional programming. This generally
means a stack based virtual machine, and a program consisting of words which are
functions taking an input stack and returning an output stack. The natural
syntax that results is postfix. Over a very long time I have come to feel that
syntax gets in between me and the power in a language. Postfix is the least
syntax possible.
There are several reasons I like the concatenative style of programming:
Function composition is concatenation.
Pipelining values through functions to get new values is the most natural
idiom.
Functions are applied from left to right instead of inside out.
Support for multiple return values comes for free.
No need for operator precedence.
Fewer delimiters are required:
Parentheses are not needed to control operator precedence.
Semicolons are not needed to separate statements.
Commas are not needed to separate arguments.
(Note: Sapf is inspired by, but is not purely a concatenative language because it has lexical variables.)
When I am programming interactively, I most often find myself in the situation
where I have a value and I want to transform it to something else. The thing to
do is apply a function with some parameters. With concatenative programming this
is very natural. You string along several words and get a new value.
QUICK SET-UP
Put the sapf program into ~/bin or wherever you keep commands.
Since this binary is unsigned you will need to remove Apple's quarantine attribute:
xattr -r -d com.apple.quarantine <path-to-sapf-binary>
Set up the environment variables in Terminal or your shell profile.
For example:
export SAPF_HISTORY="$HOME/sapf-files/sapf-history.txt"
export SAPF_LOG="$HOME/sapf-files/sapf-log.txt"
export SAPF_PRELUDE="$HOME/sapf-files/sapf-prelude.txt"
export SAPF_EXAMPLES="$HOME/sapf-files/sapf-examples.txt"
export SAPF_README="$HOME/sapf-files/README.txt"
export SAPF_RECORDINGS="$HOME/sapf-files/recordings"
export SAPF_SPECTROGRAMS="$HOME/sapf-files/spectrograms"
read this README.
check out some examples:
start sapf in Terminal.
open sapf-examples.txt in a text editor
copy an example onto the command line.
COMMAND LINE
sapf [-r sample-rate][-p prelude-file]
sapf [-h]
print this help
OPTIONS
-r sample-rate
Sets the session sample rat

data.title: U.S. has bombed Fordo nuclear plant in attack on Iran
data.author: mattcollins
data.article_summary: 美国轰炸了伊朗的福尔多等核设施，特朗普称此举为“辉煌的军事成功”，并警告伊朗若不寻求和平，将面临更严重打击。伊朗媒体证实福尔多核设施遭到攻击，但未透露具体损失。此次袭击被视为特朗普外交政策的体现，对伊朗与以色列关系产生重大影响。哈马斯谴责美国袭击为“公然侵略”，而以色列则称赞特朗普的“勇敢决定”。专家指出，美国对伊朗核设施造成了重大打击，但具体损毁情况需进一步评估。此次行动引发了对美伊冲突升级的担忧，以及特朗普是否准备推动伊朗政权更迭的猜测。

不同观点：
• 一些评论关注军事行动的直接影响和武器技术，如[tptacek]对GBU-57 "bunker buster"炸弹的描述，以及[ggm]对炸弹历史和伊朗建筑技术的讨论。这些评论聚焦于技术细节和军事能力。
• [neilv]对全球和平的期望与对历史不公的反思形成一种人道主义视角，强调对不公正行为的反思以及对和平的渴望。
• [markus_zhang]和[cedws]关注政治后果和伊朗核计划的未来，质疑这次行动是否会结束伊朗的核野心。
• [greenavocado]从地缘政治角度分析美国、中国和伊朗之间的关系，强调最近的中伊铁路链接对美国全球主导地位的挑战。
• [dkjaudyeqooe]和[duxup]警告军事行动的潜在风险和长期不稳定性，包括中东的不稳定、无休止的战争可能性以及核扩散的威胁。
• [le-mark]将事件归因于内塔尼亚胡对特朗普的影响，并预测中国和俄罗斯会借机扩大影响力，批评特朗普政府的决策能力。
• [vaughands]和[denkmoon]质疑美国行动的实际效益，[vaughands]直接质疑美国的利益所在，[denkmoon]则认为伊朗会因缺乏常规防御能力而追求核武，作为最终威慑手段。
• [Waterluvian]从个人视角反思国际政治，认为某些国家追求核武可能是对国际威胁的合理回应，质疑当今国际政治中的正义立场。

补充讨论：

data.title: Debunking NIST's calculation of the Kyber-512 security level (2023)
data.author: RA2lover
data.article_summary: 这篇文章总结了cr.yp.to博客上的一系列技术主题，涵盖从后量子加密、编译器优化到安全漏洞分析等内容。关键主题包括对Kyber-512算法门计数和NIST计算的分析与反驳，讨论了Turbo Boost技术带来的安全风险，以及对McEliece标准化的展望。此外，文章还涉及量子计算、双重加密、专利延迟推出后量子加密的原因、NSA和NIST的法律诉讼、以及对欧洲量子宣言的批评。技术细节涉及随机数生成器、向量化介绍、ROCA攻击案例研究、以及批量攻击的经济性等。整体内容强调了安全分析、算法优化及其在现实世界中的应用与挑战。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：NIST是否承认其在Kyber-512算法上的算术错误，以及对比特币挖矿计算量的讨论。

不同观点：
• [ggm] 认为，如果NIST的计算有误，应该有人提出反驳，并且在正确的情况下，NIST应该承认错误。然而，目前没有看到NIST在这方面的正式回应，因此质疑NIST是否已经正式接受其算术错误，并想知道NIST是否仍然支持Kyber-512。

• [wahern] 对评论中提到的2022年比特币挖矿仅进行了2^111次位操作的说法表示怀疑，并试图通过计算验证这一数据的真实性。通过对比特币矿工在2022年的算力数据进行估算，认为全球计算能力已经达到了令人难以置信的规模，特别是仅比特币挖矿的算力就已经如此巨大。

• [omoikane] 提供了之前关于NIST计算错误讨论的链接，暗示这个问题已经不是第一次被提及，之前就有对NIST Kyber-512安全级别计算的质疑和讨论。

• [perching_aix] 对安全领域中出现这样的算术错误表示失望，认为严肃的安全工作应该每一步都涉及机械化的数学证明，以避免此类错误。对目前这种情况表示担忧，并认为这不应该是安全工作中的常态。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于NIST是否已经正式承认其在Kyber-512算法上的算术错误，以及是否仍然支持Kyber-512。
• 对于比特币挖矿算力的讨论，焦点在于评论中提到的2^111次位操作这一数据的准确性和可信度，通过估算和对比试图验证其合理性。
• 对安全工作中出现算术错误的失望和对机械化数学证明的期望，反映出对安全领域工作流程和标准的高要求。

data.title: Application First – Media over QUIC
data.author: wofo
data.article_summary: 本文作者讲述了自己从Discord离职并专注于开发Media over QUIC项目的历程。作者曾在Twitch和Discord工作，尝试通过QUIC和WebTransport解决WebRTC的延迟问题，并创建了Warp项目，但因公司战略变化和标准化的复杂性而受阻。作者认为Media over QUIC在CDN支持方面有潜力，但现有技术如WebRTC、HLS/DASH等已能很好满足当前需求，因此需要找到用户真正关心的应用场景。作者决定成立初创公司，继续推进Media over QUIC，并将通用组件开源。尽管标准化的过程耗时且充满争议，作者仍坚信该技术的未来。
data.comments_summary: 暂无评论

44341138.article_content:
published 5/2/2025
Application First
Today was my last day at Discord.
It’s a great company with a great product and great people.
If you’re an A/V engineer in SF,
take my job
and make me proud.
My brain says I’m making a mistake, but my heart wants to kamikaze into the sun.
It’s time to double down on this passion project.
tl;dr
I’m making a startup to progress Media over QUIC.
Any generic components will be open-source.
It’s going to be sick.
Artistic interpretation of a real mood I swear.
Media over QUIC
But before I explain more, I have to bore you with some history.
I’ve been working on Media over QUIC for a long time.
My fateful project to reduce latency at Twitch was over 5 years ago (!).
We tried using WebRTC, but it just kind of sucked; it wasn’t designed for our use case.
I eventually stumbled upon QUIC/WebTransport and
pivoted once more
.
I built something called Warp as a LL-HLS replacement for Twitch and it was pretty good.
We needed more browser support and somehow had to convince Apple this was worth adding to Safari.
So I got permission to release it as an
IETF draft
despite knowing nothing about standards bodies.
And when I say “permission”, I mean we needed to get Twitch lawyers to fight against Amazon lawyers to participate in the IETF and strike down a provincial patent filed without my knowledge.
FUN TIMES WERE HAD.
Unfortunately, priorities at Twitch changed and Warp was only briefly in production for 10% of Chrome users.
Amazon finally noticed that we were losing a ton of money and the post-Covid downsizing began.
But hey, I got severance and used it to build this crude
quic.video
website while in a coffee shop in Tokyo.
I’m back in San Francisco now; a huge downgrade.
Standardization
It turned out that the Warp draft struck a chord within IETF.
Meta
and
Cisco
had both published similar drafts.
All I had to do was
combine our drafts
and boom, we’d have the start of a new standard.
The
Media over QUIC
working group was born.
It’s apparently the most active working group
with a variety of drafts
aiming to shake up the industry.
However.
HOWEVER.
I decided this was not the most productive path
.
I stopped my involvement, and I’m no longer listed as an author on the
latest moq-transport draft
.
It would have been cool to put
author of RFC9876
on my resume.
Oh well.
Trying to standardize an experimental protocol is just a huge time sink.
Arguing with multiple people from a big established company (
cough
Cisco
cough
) was a nightmare.
I was going nowhere in a hurry.
I decided it would be better to join an existing company, like
Discord
, and see if I couldn’t replace WebRTC from within.
I’m kind of a gamer and have always wanted to work at Discord.
My BFF had just become the boss of the A/V team and I was like “I’m in”.
Well that failed.
I did some neat things at Discord, like rewriting the WebRTC SFU in Rust.
But my primary passion is MoQ and it just didn’t make any product sense.
Why would you rewrite your established A/V stack for nearly zero new features?
Why not fork WebRTC (even more) instead?
Who cares about a “simpler” protocol when everything already “works”?
Discord is prioritizing the right projects and making incremental improvements.
I can’t disagree with any of the decisions and priorities.
Like I said, it’s a great company and I hope one day they’ll end up using MoQ.
But I can’t keep working on WebRTC.
There’s just too many things that I wish I could improve but I’m forced to maintain compatibility with
libwebrtc
for browser support.
It’s a lucrative dead end.
And a bitch.
LET ME OUUUUUT
Strengths First
I’m guilty of advocating for new tech just for the sake of it.
It’s how you push boundaries.
But it’s also how you pivot in a circle.
And boy do I love rewriting stuff.
It might sound obvious, but you need to figure out what a new technology is good at
before
you use it.
It could be significantly faster, or have significantly more features, or be significantly cheaper.
But it has to have
something
.

data.author: ReadCarlBarks

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Harper与Grammarly等其他语法检查工具的对比，以及对自然语言处理（NLP）技术发展历程的讨论。

不同观点：
• **oersted**：认为Harper主要依赖硬编码规则，而非传统的统计NLP方法或LLM（大语言模型）。虽然肯定了Harper的实用性，但指出LLM等新技术正在取代旧有的NLP方法，并认为不应忽视过去的经验和技术。
• **tolerance**：更倾向于使用开源工具，因为规则透明且可修改，相比之下，LLM工具的规则不够透明，可能依赖于训练数据，不如开源工具可控。
• **aDyslecticCrow**：作为长期使用Grammarly的用户，认为Harper在拼写检查方面不如Grammarly，尤其在基于句子上下文建议正确单词方面。虽然Harper比其他工具更接近其需求，但仍偏好Grammarly。
• **shortformblog**：提到另一个开源工具LanguageTool，并指出Harper的竞争对比不完全，因为未提到LanguageTool也可以本地运行。
• **pram**：认为不使用LLM是Harper的优点，批评Grammarly由于加入AI功能而变得 inconsistent（不一致）。
• **demarq**：通过实例指出Harper在语法检查上的不足，认为其规则需要更多贡献才能达到Grammarly的水平。
• **healsdata**：对Automattic的产品持怀疑态度，担心其成功后会因盈利目的而被破坏。
• **icapybara**：支持使用LLM进行语言学习工具，认为LLM在语言处理上表现优异，并反问是否见过ChatGPT犯英语错误。
• **raybb**：希望Harper有一个网站可以测试功能，而不仅是在扩展中使用，因为目前扩展存在问题。
• **loughnane**：提到另一个工具Vale，并询问是否值得转向Harper，表示对Vale的喜爱，但承认Grammarly在某些场景下更具打磨。
• **ErrorNoBrain**：不信任Grammarly，认为其隐私性差，且作为多语言用户使用体验不佳。
• **ibobev**：长期使用Grammarly，尝试Harper后认为其表现不佳，目前不值得使用。
• **krick**：关注Harper是否仅支持英语，询问是否可以扩展到其他语言，或者其框架是否过于英语特定。

补充讨论：
• **LLM与传统NLP方法的争议**：oersted指出LLM取代了传统NLP方法，但认为不应忽视过去的技术积累。icapybara则完全信任LLM，并反问ChatGPT是否犯过英语错误。
• **开源与专有工具的讨论**：tolerance和shortformblog更倾向于使用开源工具，认为规则透明且可控，而专有工具可能隐藏规则或依赖不透明的训练数据。
• **工具的实用性与扩展性**：raybb指出Harper在扩展中的问题，希望有更好的测试途径。krick关注Harper的多语言支持潜力，质疑其框架是否适合扩展到其他语言。

争议焦点：Harper是否能在功能上媲美Grammarly，以及LLM在语言检查工具中的适用性和优势。

data.title: Developing a Retro-Roguelike Game for Multiple Platforms in C
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了开发一款可在多种 vintage 和现代计算机上运行的复古 Roguelike 游戏的过程和挑战。作者最初使用 TRSE 开发环境尝试跨平台编译，但遇到了诸如 Pascal 不熟悉、文本支持不一致和 ASCII 字符映射差异等问题。随后，作者转向使用 C 语言，利用其广泛的编译器支持和低级硬件控制能力，通过条件编译来处理不同系统的差异。然而，C 语言开发也面临编译器差异和代码膨胀等问题。最终，作者决定专注于支持具备 64K 以上内存的系统，如 Commodore 64、Atari 800 和 CP/M 系统，同时包括现代平台如 Linux、Mac 和 Windows。游戏核心包括程序生成的地图，以确保每次游戏体验独特，同时节省手动绘制地图的工作。

Developing a Retro-Roguelike Game for Multiple Platforms in C
Creating a game that runs smoothly across different vintage and modern computers is a complex and ambitious challenge. Can I achieve it?
Let me tell you the story so far; the process, obstacles, and solutions involved in making a roguelike dungeon crawler playable on systems like the Commodore 64, Commodore PET, and even more constrained machines.
Watch on
YouTube
Why Build Games for Multiple Platforms?
Many enthusiasts collect old computers just for their nostalgic value. However, having these hardware collections provide playable experiences affords fresh ways to enjoy and preserve their unique quirks and capabilities.
My goal was to develop a game that can run on, if not
all,
then at least across numerous systems, utilising each machine’s features while managing constraints like memory, graphics, and input methods.
First Approach: Using TRSE to Compile for Multiple Target Systems
The journey began with
TRSE
, a development environment supporting a huge number of vintage computer systems. My plan was to develop a text-based roguelike that could run on various hardware by compiling code for each target.
Problems
TRSE is broadly based on Pascal, unfamiliar territory for me, especially when I take long breaks from the environment.
Many older computers had incomplete or inconsistent text support in TRSE libraries as most people in the community generally develop for each systems
graphics
hardware.
Differences in hardware standards like ASCII character mapping caused compatibility headaches, especially on pre-1980s machines.
Lessons Learned
Multiplatform development on vintage hardware is additionally complicated compared to today because system standards and capabilities vary widely, even from the same company, using the same processor.
Support libraries are not always fully fleshed out in ways that match your vision, or might need adaptation for different systems.
TRSE is an amazing and pretty recent voluntary project so support for certain machines needs to come from the community.
Transitioning to C for Greater Opportunity
Realising my limitations from choosing TRSE, I shifted towards programming in C. Since C compilers exist for a broad array of hardware, from calculators to mainframes, my hope was to create a universal codebase.
Anticipated benefits of C:
Wide availability of cross-compiler support.
I had experience writing portable code adaptable to multiple hardware environments.
Features for control over low-level hardware interactions when required.
Reality Check
Despite C’s portability, a fair amount of conditional code must be used to accommodate different system architectures.
Variations in compilers (e.g., CC65, Z88DK) and variable adherence to standards (C89, C99) introduce added complexity.
Managing Platform Differences Through Conditional Compilation
One of the key techniques I used was
conditional compilation
. This process involves including or excluding parts of the code depending on the target system.
Example:
#ifdef C64
// Specific code for Commodore 64
#endif
#ifdef PET
// Specific code for Commodore PET
#endif
However, this approach becomes demanding because:
Different compilers have varying syntax and features.
Each system’s memory and graphics capabilities differ.
Code can become bloated and hard to maintain.
My focus shifted from
balancing the effort needed to support many platforms versus focusing on one.
The Challenge of Hardware Limitations
Supporting multiple machines means accounting for:
Memory constraints:
e.g., I currently have a minimum 48K RAM limit, though I would love to address this for my beloved Vic 20 by utilising RAM upgrade cartridge support.
Graphics and character sets:
Some systems have custom character graphics, others don’t.
Input controls:
Many vintage machines used keyboards, not all had native joystick support.
Loading mechanisms:
From tapes to disks, resource management varies.
All this complexity led to a strategy of focusing on systems with similar capabilities , mainly those with
64K RAM or more
, such as:
Commodore 64, PET, Plus+4, Atari 800, BBC Micro
CP/M-based systems such as IMSAI and Altair
Linux, Mac, Windows (via terminal and a graphical version using Raylib)
Developing the Core Game: Levels, Map Generation, and Graphics
Hand-Crafted Dungeons to Random Map Generation
A big win was creating a
procedurally generated map
to make each gameplay experience unique and to save me having the added task of hand drawing maps in a level editor. The main downside is the ram this process takes up versus loading a complete map on level change. Fortunately, the delay for generating the map is not as long as I feared so it is not a very noticeable pause in action.
This map generator produces random but walkable layouts, and based on guard-rails in the logic, adds the baddies and collectibles throughout the level.

data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 《Tandy Corporation, Part 1》一文讲述了Tandy公司的起源与早期发展。1919年，David Lewis Tandy和Norton Hinckley创立了Hinckley-Tandy皮革公司，专营皮革制品。Tandy家族专注销售和市场，公司逐渐扩展。David的儿子Charles David Tandy在二战后创立了Tandy Leather业余爱好部门，通过邮购业务取得成功。由于经营理念分歧，Tandy家族最终掌控公司，并于1950年代快速扩展零售业务。1954年，David去世后，公司因遗产税陷入财务困境，Charles通过与一家上市公司合并解决这一问题，并最终在1959年重新掌控公司，将其更名为Tandy Corporation。之后，公司股票上市，并开始多元化经营，包括电子产品，推动公司进一步增长。

In 1919, a small leather company was founded in Fort Worth by David Lewis Tandy and Norton Hinckley. The Hinckley-Tandy Leather Company specialized in leather show laces, shoe soles, leather and rubber heels, and other shoe-findings. Tandy focused on sales and marketing while Hinckley managed the internal business operations and inventory. The company did well, bought a larger location in 1923 and expanded to Beaumont in 1927. The company scaled back during the Depression, but they survived.
Charles David Tandy
Charles David Tandy, the son of David Lewis Tandy, was born a year before Hinckley-Tandy started operations, and he began working at the company at the age of twelve. He graduated from Texas Christian University in 1940, briefly attended the Harvard Business School, and he then joined the US Navy. The younger Tandy served as a supply officer, but he also setup a leather working program for hospitalized personnel. This was successful, and it provided the inspiration for his first major contribution to Hinckley-Tandy after his discharge in 1948: Tandy Leather, a mail order hobby division of the company.
Disagreements between Hinckley and the Tandys were growing. Hinckley wanted to focus on the shoe-findings that had built the company, while the Tandys had greater ambitions. The Tandy family ended up in control of the company and the hobby division had achieved 100% ROI in its first year. In May of 1950, Charles Tandy opened the first two retail locations specialized in leather craft, but the company’s main revenues came from their mail order business. At two years, the company had achieved $2.9 million in sales, opened 15 stores, and wasn’t yet ready to stop its expansion. By 1952, the company had stores across the country, had acquired a few failing competitors, and had established an interesting method of encouraging both employees and store managers to succeed. Each store was incorporated individually, and store managers were required to own a 25% stake in the store. Should a manager lack the capital personally, Tandy Leather was available to provide the loan for that purpose, and Dave Tandy would serve as a co-signer should it be needed. For regular employees across the company, year end bonuses were provided, and all staff were eligible and encouraged to purchase equity. This worked well; by 1954, the company’s catalog was 68 pages and served a million customers, four factories stocked the shelves of 67 stores spread across 36 states and the territory of Hawaii.
While one might assume that taxation would require respiration, this is not so. In 1954, Dave Tandy passed away and the estate taxes hurt the company’s finances rather badly. This sudden shift in the company’s fortunes also meant that employee stock holders had no meaningful way to assess the value of their shares. As the remaining Tandy in our story saw it, the easiest way to ameliorate the concerns of share holders was for the company to go public. Given the company’s size, this would have been difficult, and he therefore sought a merger with an already publicly listed company.
The merger target Tandy found was the American Hide and Leather Company. AHLC was insolvent and this presented Tandy with the chance to remain in control of the resulting conglomerate. Tandy Leather provided AHLC the money to buy Tandy Leather, and Tandy Leather share holders had the option to buy shares in AHLC. This merger was completed in 1955, the company was renamed to General American Industries Inc, Tandy became the president, and the combined entity had a five year tax shelter due to AHLC’s insolvency. With AHLC as the corporate parent, profits from Tandy Leather were being used to cover the losses of other conglomerate members such as Western Leather and Tex Tan. To stop this would mean that Tandy would need to regain control. This was achieved in November of 1959.
With Tandy now in control, the unprofitable child companies were sold at a loss, the company’s headquarters was moved to Fort Worth, the conglomerate was renamed the Tandy Corporation, and the stock symbol became TAN. At open the stock was $4/share, and by the end of 1961 it was $11/share.
With ownership, earnings, taxes, and other issues settled, Tandy changed his focus back to growth. The first two initiatives were experimental retail stores Tandy Craft and Hobby Mart in November of 1961. The first stores were around 18,000 square feet, sold more than 50,000 items of varying kinds for a variety of hobbies, and notably included Electronic Crafts like DIY radio and stereo kits. Other diversification efforts continued over the decade with names like The Mart, and Pier 1 Imports.

data.title: An analysis of recent multithreading improvements for a smoother game
data.author: diggan
data.article_summary:
本文简要介绍了Arma 3在2.20更新中对多线程处理的优化，旨在提升游戏流畅度，减少卡顿和帧率波动。虽然RV引擎自Arma 2以来一直支持多线程，但此次更新对其进行了全面改进，特别关注于减少lag spike和提升最低FPS，使游戏感觉更加顺畅。更新后，最高FPS可能变化不大，甚至在超高帧率下可能略有下降，但整体游戏体验更加平滑。

文章还提到玩家在使用Profiling分支测试时因错误命令行参数导致问题，建议玩家正确设置参数，避免不必要的性能影响。例如，不需要手动设置-cpuCount来限制CPU核心数，-enableHT参数效果因硬件而异，而-exThreads参数不应使用。此次优化基于开发团队的深入研究，感谢社区的反馈和支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：游戏开发中的并行化、多线程设计及性能优化问题

不同观点：
• **[o11c]** 认为AI和脚本无法并行化的常见问题源于设计选择，即所有角色都拥有全局对象的准确信息。如果每个角色仅保存自己所需的世界信息副本，就可以实现并行化，虽然这会增加内存使用，但可以通过限制副本大小来控制。此外，建议不要在脚本API中暴露隐式访问状态的函数，而是通过显式传递对象来控制访问和修改权限，这样可以提高设计的清晰度和可维护性。

• **[egypturnash]** 提到了玩家因过时优化指南设置错误命令行参数，导致游戏多线程优化后出现问题。建议可以增加弹窗提示，警告玩家某些参数可能不再适用，并引导他们查看相关博客以获取更多信息，从而避免错误设置影响游戏体验。

• **[hinkley]** 讨论了作业系统设计对多线程利用的影响，指出旧的设计存在局限性，比如所有任务必须一次性提交并等待完成，导致效率低下（即"Fork-Join"模式）。通过改造系统，允许任务以队列形式持续运行，能够显著提升吞吐量，并且解决了某些任务集群造成的负载问题。此外，强调了突发高负载对系统的影响，建议通过自我限制流量来避免内存压力，并给自动扩展系统留出适应时间。

补充讨论：

reported by
Dedmen
on June 17, 2025
UNIT
: Dedmen, Programmer, Programming
TO
